name: Bishnupur 15th-Century Terracotta Vishnu Temple
description: Situated in the historic town of Bishnupur (ancient Lumlangdong) 27 km south of Imphal, protected by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) as a monument of national importance, constructed in 1467 CE during the reign of King Kyamba of Manipur following his joint conquest of Kyang with the King of Pong (Shan kingdom of upper Burma), recognized as the oldest surviving brick and terracotta temple in Manipur, famous for its unique single-celled sanctum topped by a corbelled curvilinear tower displaying strong Chinese and Shan pagoda architectural influences.

name: Champu Khangpok Floating Village (Loktak Phumdi Settlement)
description: Floating in the middle of Loktak Lake between Thanga and Karang islands, Champu Khangpok is an extraordinary, off-grid indigenous fishing settlement comprising around 200 households constructed entirely atop natural floating mats of decomposed vegetation, soil, and roots known as 'phumdis', recognized as a distinct revenue village with its own unique solar-powered floating primary school, traditional bamboo thatched huts ('phumsangs'), communal floating jetties, and an ancient sustainable way of life governed entirely by the rhythms of the lake.

name: Ebudhou Khoriphaba Hill & Sacred Grove (Nambol)
description: Perched on a conical green hillock in Nambol town along the boundary between Bishnupur and Imphal West districts, Ebudhou Khoriphaba Hill is an ancient Umang Lai (sacred forest deity) shrine dedicated to Khoriphaba (son of Sky God Soraren and Goddess Konthoujam Tampha), featuring a peaceful hilltop temple surrounded by preserved sacred tree groves, stone monoliths, and an annual traditional Lai Haraoba festival celebrated with vibrant ancient Meitei ritual dances and polo competitions.

name: Gopinath Temple Ningthoukhong
description: Situated in the historic town of Ningthoukhong 6 km south of Bishnupur along the Tiddim Road, the Shri Shri Gopinath Temple is one of Manipur's most sacred and historic Vaishnavite shrines, established in the late 18th century by the saint-king Maharaja Bhagyachandra (who composed the classical Manipuri Maha Raas Leela), featuring traditional Meitei-Hindu temple architecture, an open-air prayer mandapa with carved wooden pillars, an ancient holy pond, and hosting deeply devotional Raas Leela dances and Janmashtami celebrations.

name: INA War Memorial & Museum Moirang
description: Situated in the historic town of Moirang 45 km south of Imphal, revered across India as a sanctum of the Indian Independence Movement, where Colonel Shaukat Ali Malik of the Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj) hoisted the first Indian Tricolour flag on liberated Indian soil on 14 April 1944 with the support of the Japanese army, featuring an exact replica of the original 1945 Singapore INA Memorial, a life-sized bronze statue of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose, and an invaluable museum housing authentic wartime weapons, currency, uniforms, and photographic archives.

name: Ithing Island & Floating Phumsang Trail
description: Situated between Sendra Island and Thanga Island linked by a scenic elevated causeway and bridge across the open waters of Loktak Lake, Ithing is a charming, narrow hill island inhabited by traditional fishing families, celebrated for its bustling morning fish market where freshly caught Loktak fish are auctioned, traditional floating fishermen huts (phumsangs) anchored along its shores, and picturesque elevated walking paths with 360-degree views of the phumdi-carpeted lake.

name: Karang Island (India's First Cashless Island)
description: Floating like an emerald turtle in the middle of Loktak Lake accessible only by motorized country boat from Thanga jetty, Karang is a picturesque Meitei fishermen's island village that gained international fame in January 2017 when the Government of India declared it as India's first 100% cashless island, renowned for its tranquil village lanes, solar-powered homes, panoramic lake vistas, and centuries-old traditional fishing lifestyle using reed traps.

name: Keibul Lamjao National Park
description: Located in the Bishnupur district of Manipur, Keibul Lamjao National Park is the world's only floating national park, situated on the Loktak Lake. This park is renowned for its unique ecosystem, which supports a wide variety of flora and fauna, including the endangered Sangai deer, also known as the brow-antlered deer or dancing deer. The park's floating wetlands, known as 'phumdis,' provide a natural habitat for various species of birds, making it a paradise for birdwatchers and nature lovers. With its breathtaking scenery and diverse wildlife, Keibul Lamjao National Park offers an unforgettable experience for visitors, allowing them to connect with nature and unwind in the midst of Manipur's serene mountains. The park's cultural significance is also evident in its connection to the local communities, who have traditionally relied on the park's resources for their livelihood.

name: Khoirok Thong & Thongjaorok Historic Stone Bridges
description: Spanning the turbulent mountain stream of Thongjaorok in the foothills near Bishnupur and Khoirok, these ancient stone bridges (including Khoirok Thong and Thongjaorok Bridge) are remarkable engineering relics from the Ningthouja royal dynasty, constructed out of massive hand-chiseled quartzite boulders and dressed stone slabs using ancient dry-stone corbelling techniques without mortar, engineered to withstand violent monsoon flash floods roaring down from the western hills.

name: Kumbi Keibul River Confluence & Ancient Shrines
description: Situated at the southern boundary of Bishnupur district bordering Churachandpur along the Khuga River just 10 km south of Moirang, Kumbi is an ancient Meitei settlement nestled beside Keibul Lamjao National Park, celebrated for its historic sacred shrines dedicated to Ibudhou Sanakhwa Kumbi and Iputhou Pakhangba, scenic riverside promenades, and traditional handloom and pottery craft.

name: Laimaton Parallel Point & Laimaton Ridge
description: Perched at an elevation of over 1,800 meters along the crest of the rugged Laimaton mountain range on the western frontier of Bishnupur district, Laimaton Parallel Point is an extraordinary scenic high-altitude ridge overlook, celebrated among adventure trekkers and landscape photographers for offering peerless 360-degree panoramic vistas encompassing the entire emerald expanse of Loktak Lake, the meandering rivers of the Imphal valley, and the misty blue folds of the Leimatak gorge.

name: Loktak Canal & Hiyang Tanaba Traditional Boat Race Arena
description: Stretching as an engineered hydraulic waterway linking Loktak Lake with the royal settlement of Ningthoukhong, the Loktak Canal is celebrated in Manipuri sporting history as the official venue for 'Hiyang Tannaba' (the ancient Meitei traditional boat race), where long, slender dugout racing canoes ('Hiyang') bearing elaborately carved wooden dragon and horned creature prows compete fiercely in royal regattas under traditional rules dating back centuries.

name: Loktak Folklore Museum (Thanga Tongbram)
description: Perched on a scenic hillock in Thanga Tongbram on Thanga Island within Loktak Lake, founded in 2016 through the visionary personal initiative of local folklorist Tongbram Sahadeve, the Loktak Folklore Museum is an extraordinary grassroots community museum dedicated to preserving the unique oral folklore, traditional fishing implements, ancestral terracotta pottery, indigenous weaving looms, and vintage aquatic artifacts of the Loktak fishing community.

name: Loktak Lake
description: Loktak Lake is famous for its floating islands called phumdis and is one of the most unique landscapes in India. It is also home to the endangered Sangai deer.

name: Lord Thangjing Temple Moirang
description: Situated in the ancient cultural town of Moirang, Lord Thangjing Temple is one of the most sacred primordial religious shrines in Manipur, dedicated to Ibudhou Thangjing (the supreme presiding deity of the ancient kingdom of Moirang), celebrated in folklore as the mythical setting of the epic romance of Khamba and Thoibi (the Meitei Romeo and Juliet), and recognized as the original ancestral cradle where the sacred Meitei ritual dance festival of Moirang Lai Haraoba is celebrated with centuries-old dances every May.

name: Loukoi Pat Eco-Park & Ecological Lake Bishnupur
description: Situated just 800 meters from the historic Vishnu Temple in Bishnupur town 27 km south of Imphal, Loukoi Pat is an enchanting ecological lake cradled in a natural basin surrounded by verdant hillocks, developed into an eco-tourism park featuring lotus-filled waters, pedal and row boating, winding hill trails, scenic resting gazebos, and an elevated viewpoint offering sweeping vistas over the Bishnupur plains.

name: Moirang Kangla & Khamba-Thoibi Cultural Heritage Site
description: Situated in the heart of Moirang near the INA Memorial, Moirang Kangla is the ancient consecrated citadel and royal coronation seat of the historic Moirang principality (one of the seven ancestral Meitei salais/clans), celebrated in Manipuri literature as the epic stage of the legendary romantic saga of 'Khamba and Thoibi' (the Romeo and Juliet of Manipur), preserving ancient stone coronation plinths, sacred ritual grounds, and the vibrant open-air festival arena for the world-famous Moirang Lai Haraoba.

name: Nachou Lakeside Waterfront & Sunset Pier
description: Located along the tranquil western shoreline of Loktak Lake at Nachou village, just 3 km east of Bishnupur town, Nachou Waterfront is an open, undeveloped lakeshore embankment where the waters of Loktak meet expansive grazing meadows, celebrated by local photographers for offering some of the most spectacular, unobstructed sunset vistas in the valley as the evening sun sinks behind the dark silhouette of the western hill ranges, silhouetting solitary fishermen in their canoes.

name: Ningthoukhong Historic Royal Residence & Water Channels
description: Situated on the western shores of Loktak Lake 32 km south of Imphal in Bishnupur district, Ningthoukhong is an ancient historic settlement that served as a royal secondary residence and defense outpost of the Ningthouja kings, famous for its ancient canal water system ('Khong'), historic shrines of the local presiding deity Ibudhou Oknarel, and housing the primary powerhouse and switchyard of the NHPC Loktak Hydroelectric Project.

name: Oinam Heritage Settlement & Handloom Weaving
description: Situated along the Tiddim Road (NH-2) in Bishnupur district 20 km south of Imphal, Oinam is an ancient Meitei settlement renowned across Manipur as a primary center of indigenous handloom textile craftsmanship, where skilled women weavers use traditional wooden fly-shuttle and backstrap loin-looms to weave exquisite cotton and silk Phaneks, Inaphis, and ceremonial shawls, home to ancient sacred ponds and ancestral shrines.

name: Oinam Mandha Hillock & Rural Wetland Viewpoint
description: Rising dramatically from the flat agricultural plains of Oinam along National Highway 2 (Tiddim Road) in northern Bishnupur district, Oinam Mandha is an isolated quartzite hillock that acts as a natural observation tower over the surrounding countryside, offering panoramic views of geometric green paddy mosaics, meandering branches of the Nambol river, and the distant silvery shimmer of Loktak Lake against the blue western hills.

name: P.P. Park & Eco-Recreation Grounds Bishnupur
description: Situated in the southern outskirts of Bishnupur town near the foothills, P.P. Park is a popular local ecological recreation garden and family park, featuring landscaped green terraces, vibrant seasonal flowerbeds of marigolds and dahlias, children's joy rides, shaded bamboo gazebos, walking pathways, and tranquil views of the forested western hills.

name: Phubala & Komlakhong Water Sports Waterfront
description: Situated along the western shoreline of Loktak Lake between Nambol and Moirang 40 km from Imphal, Phubala and Komlakhong form a tranquil lakefront corridor highlighted in the Manipur Tourism Policy for water sports and ecotourism, featuring low-lying grassy shores extending into the lake, birdwatching shelters overlooking flocks of migratory pintails and coots, pedal boating, and tranquil picnic groves.

name: Red Hill (Maibam Lokpa Ching) & Imphal Peace Museum
description: Situated on a prominent red-soiled hillock at Maibam Lokpa Ching in Nambol along the Tiddim Road (NH-2) 16 km south of Imphal, celebrated in military history as the site of the ferocious Battle of Red Hill between 21 and 29 May 1944 where British Fourteenth Army and Gurkha forces halted the Japanese 33rd Division in intense hand-to-hand combat, featuring the serene India Peace Memorial erected by the Government of Japan in 1994, and the world-class Imphal Peace Museum inaugurated in June 2019 on the 75th anniversary of the battle.

name: Sangai Ethnic Park Moirangkhunou
description: Inaugurated in November 2022 near Keibul Lamjao National Park at Moirangkhunou, developed as the grand permanent main venue for the annual Manipur Sangai Festival, sprawling across picturesque lakefront grounds featuring authentic life-sized replica huts and architectural dwellings representing all 34 recognized Meitei and tribal communities of Manipur, traditional morungs, an open-air amphitheatre, and handloom craft exhibition pavilions.

name: Sendra Island & Tourist Resort
description: Perched on an elevated, conical volcanic hillock rising from the shimmering sapphire waters of Loktak Lake 48 km south of Imphal, connected to the mainland by a scenic causeway road, celebrated as the premier panoramic vantage point for viewing the vast circular floating biomass islands ('Phumdis'), featuring the Sendra Tourist Home operated by Manipur Tourism with observation towers, fine ethnic dining, and direct boat jetty departures.

name: Siddheswar Temple Bishnupur
description: Perched on a scenic, pine-clad hillock overlooking Bishnupur town just west of the historic terracotta Vishnu Temple, Shri Siddheswar Temple is an ancient and revered shrine dedicated to Lord Shiva, featuring a natural stone Shiva Lingam nestled in a tranquil forest clearing, surrounded by blooming wild orchids, ancient stone steps, and commanding sweeping panoramic vistas across the lush paddy plains of Bishnupur toward the shimmering blue waters of Loktak Lake.

name: T. Mongbung Dam & Waroiching Stream
description: Tucked into the emerald forested foothills near Waroiching and Leimaram in northern Bishnupur district, T. Mongbung Dam is a quiet freshwater irrigation reservoir fed by the pristine mountain runoff of the Waroiching stream, surrounded by dense bamboo groves, sloping forested hillocks, and quiet pebble-strewn riverbanks that provide an idyllic natural picnic haven for local families and birdwatchers.

name: Takmu Water Sports Complex & Rowing Channel
description: Situated on the calm, protected waters of Takmu Lake (an inlet of the larger Loktak Lake system) adjacent to Sendra Island in Moirang, developed as a premier national-level water sports facility by the Department of Youth Affairs and Sports, equipped with international-standard rowing, canoeing, and kayaking channels, motorboats, speedboats, and spectator pavilions, host to multiple National Games water sports events.

name: Thanga Island & Omba Ching Ridge
description: Extending as a picturesque cluster of rolling volcanic hillocks directly into the heart of Loktak Lake 50 km south of Imphal, Thanga is a vibrant Meitei fishermen's island peninsula (comprising Thanga Chingkha, Thanga Chinglak, and Omba Ching), celebrated for its traditional lakeside homestays, winding ridge roads with endless water views, dramatic morning sunrises illuminating floating phumdis, and ancient shrines dedicated to the lake deities.

name: Thangjing Hill Trail & Forest Shrine
description: Soaring to an elevation of approximately 2,100 meters (6,890 feet) in the Thangjing range directly west of Moirang, Thangjing Hill (Thangjing Ching) is the deeply sacred celestial abode of Ebudhou Thangjing, the supreme guardian deity of the ancient kingdom of Moirang, featuring an ancient mountain-crest stone altar where traditional Meitei pilgrims undertake an arduous ritual trek through dense oak and rhododendron forests during the annual Thangjing Ching Kaba pilgrimage to offer prayers for universal prosperity.

name: Upper Sadu Chiru Natural Pools & Forest Cascades
description: Located in the rugged, densely forested mountain gorge above the main tourist falls of Sadu Chiru (Leimaram Falls) in the western foothills near Leimaram, the Upper Sadu Chiru cascades consist of a sequence of pristine natural rock pools, narrow moss-draped gorges, and hidden multi-tier waterfalls that remain wild and untouched beyond the reach of concrete tourist staircases, fed by perennial sub-Himalayan mountain springs flowing through lush ferns and wild ginger groves.

name: Chakpi River Gorges & Rocky Rapids (Chakpikarong)
description: Flowing southwards through the heart of southern Chandel before cutting across the hills toward Myanmar, the Chakpi River around Chakpikarong has sculpted dramatic gorges, crystalline cascades, white pebble beaches, and sculpted bedrock pools, surrounded by dense semi-evergreen forest canopies where the clear mountain river provides popular seasonal picnic beaches, river angling spots, and tranquil forest walking trails.

name: Chakpikarong Scenic River Bend Chandel
description: Situated in a scenic river valley in southern Chandel district 15 km south of Chandel town and 80 km from Imphal, Chakpikarong is a charming hill town built around a wide, graceful bend of the crystal-clear Chakpi River, celebrated for its historic wire-rope suspension footbridges spanning the river, excellent sport angling for indigenous freshwater mahseer, pebble beaches, and surrounding teak-covered hills.

name: Chandel Town Hilltop & St. Peter's Cathedral
description: Perched on a scenic, undulating mountain ridge 64 km southeast of Imphal, Chandel town (formerly Chamdil) is the charming administrative headquarters of Chandel district, renowned for its cool mountain climate, vibrant tribal morning markets selling wild mushrooms, fermented bamboo shoots, and hill honey, and the soaring white facade of St. Peter's Cathedral crowning the hill, commanding sweeping views over the surrounding forested valleys.

name: Doyang Caves & Yangdung Karst Formations
description: Hidden deep in the forested limestone hills of the Khenjoi-Yangdung sector near Khongtan in southern Chandel district, the Doyang Caves are an untouched, subterranean karst cave system featuring towering calcite stalactites, multi-chambered flowstone formations, narrow crawlways, and colony roosts of rare roundleaf bats, preserved in near-total wilderness and regarded by regional speleologists as one of the most promising unexplored cave systems in the Indo-Burma biodiversity hotspot.

name: Gamvet Muol (Lilybung Hilltop Ridge)
description: Rising prominently over the Chakpikarong basin in southern Chandel, Gamvet Muol (popularly known as Lilybung) is a picturesque, wind-swept mountain ridge characterized by rolling grassy hillocks, seasonal blooms of rare wild mountain lilies, rocky crags, and panoramic vistas commanding the Chakpi river valley and the undulating blue contours of the Indo-Myanmar frontier hills, serving as a cherished destination for local hikers and 4WD off-road enthusiasts.

name: Joupi Hills & Forest Wilderness
description: Perched atop scenic, breeze-kissed mountain ridges in southern Chandel along the highway to the border, Joupi is an atmospheric hill settlement enveloped by dense native teak, bamboo, and oak forests, offering breathtaking panoramic vistas of the rolling blue hills of the Indo-Myanmar frontier, crisp clean mountain air, and serving as a crucial ecological stepping stone for migrating avian species and wildlife.

name: Kana River Confluence & Sandbars (Moltuh Valley)
description: Situated near Moltuh village in the southern reaches of Chandel district where the Kana Lok river converges with mountain streams flowing from the Khenjoi hills, this scenic river confluence is renowned for its wide white sandbars, tranquil turquoise pools, and gentle pebble shallows framed by dramatic sub-tropical jungle bluffs, serving as an idyllic natural retreat for wilderness camping, angling, and river bathing.

name: Kanat River Valley & Subterranean Caverns
description: Flowing through deep limestone canyons in the remote southern folds of Chandel district, the Kanat River has carved an enchanting aquatic wilderness featuring hidden karst caverns, natural limestone grottoes accessible only by wading through crystal-clear mountain waters, dramatic overhanging cliff walls, and deep natural rock pools teeming with indigenous hill-stream fishes.

name: Kathong Chingjao Hill Range & Haubiching Peak
description: Dominating the central skyline of Chandel district, Kathong Chingjao is a monumental, densely forested mountain range culminating in the sacred rocky crags of Haubiching peak, renowned in regional history as a natural fortress during historical inter-tribal conflicts and royal Burmese border campaigns, preserving virgin oak and rhododendron canopies, hidden cave systems, and commanding sweeping vistas across southern Manipur.

name: Khenjoi Hills & Wildlife Reserve Frontier
description: Sprawling across a vast, rugged sub-division along the southern international border with Myanmar, the Khenjoi Hills comprise one of the largest contiguous blocks of untouched rainforest and subtropical broadleaf forest in Manipur, officially highlighted by the district administration for its immense ecotourism potential, harboring healthy wild populations of clouded leopards, Malayan sun bears, Great Indian Hornbills, and rare orchids.

name: Liwa Changning & Monsang Pantha Heritage Villages
description: Located just 2 km outside Chandel town along the banks of the scenic river, Liwa Changning and Monsang Pantha are ancient cultural villages of the Monsang and Anal Naga communities, celebrated for their traditional bamboo and timber stilt architecture, terraced paddy fields, sacred community groves, master cane and bamboo artisans weaving intricate headgear and fishing baskets, and vibrant performances of the traditional Monsang folk dances.

name: Machi Historical Maring Naga Village Chandel
description: Perched on a scenic, pine-fringed mountain ridge in northern Chandel district 25 km east of Kakching, Machi is celebrated as the ancient ancestral mother village of the Maring Naga tribe (the 'Black Hair-Bun Tribe'), famous for retaining centuries-old customs where male elders traditionally wear high woven braided topknots ('Khongchet'), handloom black-and-red geometric shawls, ancient megalithic stone circles, and traditional bamboo and woodcrafts.

name: Molcham Indo-Myanmar Gateway & Border Frontier
description: Situated in the extreme southern tip of Chandel district right on the international border with Myanmar (Sagaing Region), Molcham is an internationally significant frontier settlement affectionately known as the 'Gateway to India', marking the historic southern land trade route connecting Manipur with Burma, featuring the official Gateway to India memorial arch, international border boundary pillars, border security checkpoints, and sweeping views of the Chin Hills across the frontier.

name: Peace Island Chandel & River Picnic Grounds
description: Nestled along the riverbed just south of Chandel town, Peace Island is a picturesque, naturally formed river island created by the bifurcating waters of the clear mountain stream, densely shaded by weeping willows, bamboo clumps, and wild fig trees, equipped with stone seating, stepping-stone footbridges, and shallow gravel banks that make it the most popular weekend picnic and angling haven for residents of the district.

name: Phuikon Haosabee Caves (I & II) & Prehistoric Rock Shelters
description: Discovered in the dense limestone karst ridges of Kathong Chingjao near Phuikon village, Phuikon Haosabee Caves (designated Cave-I and Cave-II) are significant prehistoric archaeological sites documented by the Manipur State Archaeology Department, featuring vaulted limestone chambers with natural stone pillars, calcified flowstones, and evidence of ancient human occupation, animal bone remains, and stone-age rock shelters utilized by prehistoric inhabitants of the valley.

name: Phuikon Ningthou Cave & Khommunnom Rock Shelter
description: Situated in the rugged hills of the Kathong Chingjao formation near Khommunnom, Phuikon Ningthou Cave ('King's Cave') is an imposing natural limestone cavern revered in local Anal and Maring tribal folklore as the ancient hiding sanctuary and council chamber of tribal chieftains, while the adjacent Khommunnom Rock Shelter preserves dry overhangs, natural stone seats, and ancient petroglyph carvings dating back centuries.

name: Sajik Tampak Valley & Limestone Caves
description: Situated in a broad, scenic mountain valley 35 km south of Chakpikarong along the sparkling Kana Lok river, Sajik Tampak is an idyllic highland basin surrounded by towering limestone cliffs, lush paddy fields, and dense sub-tropical pine forests, celebrated by adventurous travelers for its network of undiscovered natural limestone caves, dramatic hanging cliff rock formations, crystal-clear river gravel bars, and peaceful Kuki and Zou tribal hamlets.

name: Sarangba Natural Salt Springs
description: Tucked away in a scenic ravine in the Chandel hill tract near Sarangba, these ancient natural saline brine springs are of profound historical and cultural importance to Manipur, having served for centuries as one of the royal salt extraction sites where local tribal villagers boiled brine in earthen pots to produce circular crystalline salt cakes ('Meitei Thum') used as sacred currency and royal tribute for the kings of Manipur.

name: Behiang Border Trading Point & Zokhawthar Gateway
description: Situated in the southernmost tip of Churachandpur district 62 km south of Lamka, Behiang is a historic frontier village located directly on the international border with Myanmar (Chin State) at the southern terminus of National Highway 102B (Tedim Road), recognized as a designated Border Haat trading center, featuring international boundary pillars, vibrant border trade exchanges, and sweeping views across the Tuivai river gorge into the forested Chin Hills.

name: Churachandpur Town (Lamka) & Tribal Craft Markets
description: Situated 60 km southwest of Imphal along the Tiddim Road (NH-2), Churachandpur (locally known as Lamka) is the second-largest urban center and principal commercial metropolis of southern Manipur, celebrated as the vibrant cultural, intellectual, and musical capital of the Kuki, Zomi, Hmar, Paite, and Chin communities, famous for bustling tribal handloom markets selling exquisite multi-colored Paite Puandum and Thangsuang shawls, woodcrafts, and vibrant celebrations of the post-harvest Kut Festival on 1 November.

name: Gothol Waterfall & Natural Forest Basin
description: Tucked into the rugged, pine-and-oak forested hills of Gothol village about 14 km southwest of Churachandpur town, Gothol Waterfall is an enchanting natural cascade pouring over a sheer rocky ledge into a deep, serene natural swimming amphitheatre, surrounded by lush riverine ferns, blooming wild ginger, and cool mountain breezes that make it a favorite offbeat haven for local nature lovers.

name: Henglep Remote Highland Town & Bamboo Forests
description: Perched on a high, remote mountain ridge in northwestern Churachandpur district 55 km from Churachandpur town, Henglep is an atmospheric sub-divisional hill town of the Kuki tribe, renowned for its vast wild Muli bamboo forests, deep river gorges carved by mountain streams flowing toward the Barak, panoramic vistas of the Thangjing hill range, and traditional cane and bamboo craftsmanship.

name: Kaihlam Caves & Wildlife Forest Ridge
description: Perched on a high, densely forested mountain ridge in Singhat sub-division of southern Churachandpur district 45 km from Churachandpur town, Kaihlam is celebrated as a significant geological and wildlife sanctuary, featuring an extensive natural limestone cave network with calcified stalactites, enveloped in virgin oak and bamboo cloud forests that shelter Blyth's Tragopans, Leopard Cats, and rare mountain orchids.

name: Khousabung Village (Pineapple Festival & Queen Orchards)
description: Situated in the gentle fertile foothills of northern Churachandpur district 12 km west of Moirang, Khousabung is celebrated across Northeast India as the ancestral 'Pineapple Cradle of Manipur', where commercial cultivation of the prized organic Queen variety of pineapple was first introduced in 1947, featuring vast rolling hill slopes blanketed in emerald pineapple bushes, host of the famous annual State Level Manipur Pineapple Festival every August-September.

name: Khuga Dam & Multipurpose Reservoir at Mata
description: Constructed across the Khuga River at Mata village 8 km south of Churachandpur town, Khuga Dam is an imposing composite earth-fill and concrete multipurpose dam commissioned in November 2010, creating an immense, breathtaking sapphire-blue water reservoir that snakes through green mountain folds, featured in the state tourism policy for water sports, speed boating, recreational angling for local carp, and sunset lakeside promenades.

name: Khuga Reservoir Backwater Bends & Eco-Camping Fingers
description: Stretching for kilometers into the secluded mountain ravines south of the main Khuga Dam barrage, the upstream backwater fingers of the Khuga Reservoir form an enchanting, fjord-like aquatic landscape where calm, deep blue lake waters wind between steep forested hillsides, offering completely tranquil, non-commercialized inlets prized by wilderness campers, kayak enthusiasts, and freshwater anglers seeking Mahseer and hill trout.

name: Mata Dam & Riverbed (Khuga Downstream Gravel Banks)
description: Located directly downstream of the monumental Khuga Dam barrage at Mata village 8 km south of Churachandpur town, Mata Dam and its surrounding riverbed offer a tranquil, unhurried alternative to the main reservoir, featuring wide pebble and gravel banks along the gentle Khuga River, calm crystal-clear shallows, rolling grassy hill slopes, and panoramic viewpoints overlooking the southern hill ranges.

name: Mualnuam Highland Town & Mountain Forest Ridge
description: Perched at an elevation of over 1,300 meters on the western mountain backbone of Churachandpur along the road connecting Singngat to Thanlon, Mualnuam is an enchanting highland sub-divisional settlement surrounded by pristine temperate broadleaf forests, terraced hillside farming hamlets, crystal mountain streams, and rolling mist-shrouded peaks that offer cool mountain relief and sweeping vistas of the remote southern ranges.

name: Ngaloi Waterfall & Forest Stream
description: Nestled in a serene forested valley near Ngaloi village just 9 km from Churachandpur town center, Ngaloi Waterfall is celebrated as one of southern Manipur's most popular natural getaways, where a crystal mountain stream tumbles over several rocky ledges into a wide, clear natural plunge pool shaded by towering forest canopies, equipped with timber footbridges, scenic viewpoints, and riverside picnic pavilions.

name: Rengkai Historic Hmar Cultural Settlement
description: Forming an integral southern suburb of Churachandpur town, Rengkai is celebrated as the cultural and literary heartland of the Hmar people in Manipur, established in the mid-20th century and renowned for its grand stone churches with soaring spires, vibrant cultural societies, handloom clusters producing world-renowned Hmar puan shawls, and active celebrations of Sikpui Ruoi (the winter post-harvest festival).

name: Sangaikot Foothill Valley & Orange Groves
description: Situated in a scenic, fertile foothill basin 18 km south of Churachandpur town along the road to Sugnu, Sangaikot is an agricultural sub-division celebrated for its extensive organic Mandarin orange orchards, sweet sugarcane fields, rolling green pastures, traditional Kuki and Zou tribal villages, and peaceful riverfront picnic spots along the Khuga river plain.

name: Sielmat Hilltop Viewpoints & Historic Mission Heritage
description: Occupying a scenic elevated hill spur on the northern fringes of Lamka, Sielmat is of profound cultural and educational significance to the Hmar community, established as a pioneering Christian mission center in 1910 by missionary Watkin Roberts and local converts, featuring historic mission stone churches, peaceful academic compounds, traditional handloom weaving households, and hilltop viewing pathways offering panoramic views of the entire Lamka valley.

name: Singhat Frontier Town & Southern Kuki Hills
description: Perched amidst rolling pine and oak hills in southern Churachandpur district 32 km south of Churachandpur town along the strategic Guite Road (NH-102B) toward the Myanmar border, Singhat is a picturesque sub-divisional hill town of the Zou, Simte, and Paite tribes, celebrated for its cool mountain climate, traditional Christian churches, hillside ginger and turmeric terraces, and scenic mountain pass vistas.

name: Singngat Foothill Trails & Tedim Road Pine Forests
description: Nestled along the historic Tedim Road (NH-102B) in southwestern Churachandpur 30 km from Lamka, Singngat is a peaceful sub-divisional hill town situated in a scenic mountain basin surrounded by dense stands of native pine trees, cool perennial hill streams, rolling green hills, and traditional Paite and Zou tribal villages, offering picturesque off-the-beaten-track foothill walking tracks and riverbank picnic sites.

name: Suangdoh Ridge & Highlands (Tipaimukh Highway Overlook)
description: Perched at an elevation of over 1,400 meters along the historic Guite Road (NH-102B) heading toward Thanlon and Tipaimukh, Suangdoh is an atmospheric highland tribal settlement famous for its sweeping mountain ridgeline vistas, dramatic early-morning sea-of-clouds inversions filling the deep river valleys below, stepped mountain agriculture, and cool year-round climate.

name: Tonglon Cave & Archaeological Rock Shelters
description: Situated in the rugged limestone hills of southern Churachandpur district near Tonglon village 30 km from Churachandpur town, Tonglon Cave is celebrated in the state's official tourism inventory as an ancient subterranean karst cavern network, featuring multiple interconnected stone galleries adorned with calcified stalactites, stalagmites, natural stone pillars, and historical rock shelters used by ancient tribal clans.

name: Tonglon Hidden Waterfall & Jungle Stream
description: Hidden deep within dense sub-tropical foliage in the hills of Tonglon village in Singngat sub-division, downstream from the famed Tonglon limestone caves, this multi-tiered forest waterfall tumbles over moss-covered limestone ledges into a series of crystal-clear jade-green rock basins, shaded by towering wild banana and teak trees and reached via an unpaved hiking trail through rural tribal hamlets.

name: Tuila Stream & Riverbed Picnic Spots
description: Flowing through pristine oak and bamboo forested ravines along the mountain slopes crossing the Tedim Road in southern Churachandpur, the Tuila stream is a scenic perennial mountain tributary characterized by giant water-sculpted granite boulders, crystal-clear wading shallows, small sparkling waterfalls, and shaded sandy nooks that provide one of the most refreshing natural swimming and picnic spots in the district.

name: Tuivai River Gorge & Rocky Rapids (Southern Frontier)
description: Carving a colossal natural canyon along the southwestern border separating Manipur from Mizoram and Myanmar, the Tuivai River is one of the most magnificent wild mountain rivers of the Northeast, featuring roaring turquoise rapids, deep limestone gorges, towering rock cliffs draped in subtropical rainforest, and secluded pebble beaches that provide world-class opportunities for wilderness river trekking, white-water kayaking, and angling.

name: Zenhang Lamka & Traditional Cane-Bamboo Craft Clusters
description: Situated in the central core of Churachandpur town, Zenhang Lamka is a bustling commercial and artisan neighborhood celebrated as the primary center for indigenous cane and bamboo handicrafts, where generations of skilled artisans handcraft durable bamboo lounge chairs, cane baskets, fish traps, and home decor, while the evening street market comes alive with stalls offering local smoked pork delicacies, steamed tapioca, and tribal herbal snacks.

name: Zogam Tribal Museum & Cultural Heritage Centre (Tuibong)
description: Situated in the administrative quarter of Tuibong in Churachandpur, the Zogam Tribal Museum is the premier cultural repository dedicated to preserving the diverse material heritage of the indigenous Kuki-Zomi-Hmar-Mizo communities of southern Manipur, exhibiting rare antique brass gongs (Daha), traditional muzzle-loading flintlock guns, tiger bone ornaments, hornbill feather headdresses, ancient bamboo craft implements, and authentic hand-woven tribal shawls representing all local clans.

name: Andro Heritage Village
description: Andro is an ancient heritage village located at the foothills of the Nongmaiching range in Imphal East district, Manipur. It is globally famous for its unique style of pottery called 'Charai Taba', made exclusively by married women using a special wooden bat instead of a wheel. The village features the Mutua Museum, a cultural hub displaying traditional doll houses, tribal clothing, and historic artifacts from Manipur's tribes.

name: Andro Sacred Fire Sanctuary (Mei Mutaba) & Ancient Inscription Site
description: Located within the sacred precinct of the Panam Ningthou temple in Andro village, the Sacred Fire Place (Mei Mutaba) is one of the most remarkable living cultural phenomena in India—an eternal sacred fire that has been meticulously kept burning day and night without interruption by designated village households taking turns for centuries, accompanied by ancient stone pillar inscriptions dating to the reign of King Poireiton and sacred copper ritual hearths.

name: Baruni Ching (Nongmaiching Hill Peak & Sacred Pilgrimage Trail)
description: Dominating the eastern horizon of the Imphal valley with an elevation of nearly 1,500 meters, Baruni Ching (the summit ridge of Nongmaiching Hill) is one of Manipur's most sacred geographic landmarks, venerated since pre-Hindu antiquity as the sacred residence of Nongpok Ningthou (the Lord of the East) and Panthoibi, and later Lord Shiva, drawing tens of thousands of pilgrims during the annual Baruni Ching-Kaba night pilgrimage to climb its forested slopes and watch dawn break over a sea of clouds.

name: Bijali Leikol & Kombirei Wetland Gardens
description: Situated in the serene wetland canal fringes of eastern Imphal near Yaralpat, Bijali Leikol is a specialized ecological floral sanctuary and wetland garden dedicated to preserving Kombirei (Iris bakeri / Iris laevigata)—the sacred indigenous purple iris deeply woven into Meitei folklore and indispensable to the traditional Cheiraoba (Manipuri New Year) celebrations, blooming in breathtaking purple carpets across tranquil marshy beds in early spring.

name: City Convention Centre (Palace Compound)
description: Situated prominently in the historic Palace Compound in Imphal East, the City Convention Centre is Manipur's flagship modern institutional landmark for cultural diplomacy, international film festivals, classical Manipuri dance congresses, and performing arts summits, featuring a monumental glass-and-steel facade integrated with Meitei stylistic elements, an acoustically engineered 1,200-seat auditorium, art galleries, and manicured civic plazas.

name: Dolaithabi Dam & Barrage Imphal East
description: Situated across the sparkling Iril River at Dolaithabi in northern Imphal East district 24 km from central Imphal, commissioned in 2019, Dolaithabi Barrage is a major water-resource engineering project designed to irrigate over 7,500 hectares of valley farmland, featuring an imposing multi-bay concrete spillway barrage flanked by verdant pine-forested foothills, popular for scenic waterside strolling, river recreation, and countryside photography.

name: Hatta Golapati War Cemetery
description: Situated at Hatta Golapati in Imphal East along the road to Porompat 2 km from Kangla Fort, maintained by the Commonwealth War Graves Commission (CWGC), commemorating 868 brave Muslim soldiers of the British Indian Army and Royal Indian Army Service Corps who made the supreme sacrifice defending Imphal against the Japanese forces during the 1944 Battle of Imphal, featuring pristine lawn terraces, headstones oriented toward Mecca, and a commemorative pavilion.

name: Heingang Ching Foothills & Manipuri Pony Grazing Grounds
description: Spreading across the gentle slopes and green commons beneath the sacred Marjing Polo shrine in Heingang 7 km north of Imphal, these historic grazing grounds have for centuries nurtured the legendary Manipuri Pony—the purebred athletic steed on which modern polo (Sagol Kangjei) was born, featuring undulating hillock trails, quiet pony pastures, traditional Meitei sacred groves (Umang Lai), and panoramic views overlooking the Lamphel and northern valley wetlands.

name: Ibudhou Marjing Polo Hill & Colossal Polo Statue
description: Perched on the sacred summit of Heingang Hill 8 km northeast of central Imphal, revered in Meitei mythology as the celestial abode of Lord Ibudhou Marjing (the primordial deity who invented polo / Sagol Kangjei), crowned in January 2023 by the colossal 122-foot-tall bronze statue of a traditional Meitei polo player mounted on a galloping Manipuri pony, celebrated as the world's tallest statue of a polo player, offering breathtaking panoramic vistas of the Imphal valley.

name: Ima Panam Ningthou Temple Andro
description: Situated in the ancient ancestral village of Andro at the foot of the Nongmaiching hill range 25 km east of Imphal, this sacred primordial Meitei shrine is dedicated to Lord Panam Ningthou, revered across Manipur for housing the eternal sacred hearth fire ('Mei') that according to ancient royal chronicles has been kept burning continuously by rotating village families day and night since the reign of King Nongda Lairen Pakhangba in 33 CE without ever being extinguished.

name: Imphal War Cemetery (CWGC 1944 Battle of Imphal)
description: Situated at Dewlahland along the Imphal-Dimapur Road in Imphal East, meticulously maintained by the Commonwealth War Graves Commission (CWGC), commemorating 1,600 British, Indian, African, Canadian, and Australian soldiers who fell during the ferocious Battle of Imphal between March and July 1944 when the British Fourteenth Army under General Slim halted the Japanese U-Go invasion, featuring manicured emerald lawns, formal flowerbeds, and bronze-inscribed stone markers.

name: Iril River Pebble Banks & Shikhong Fringe
description: Meandering through the verdant agricultural valleys of Imphal East between Dolaithabi and Sawombung, the Iril River features sweeping gravel beaches, rounded river pebbles, crystal-clear cold mountain water flowing down from the Senapati highlands, and bamboo-shaded riverbanks, offering an idyllic, tranquil country escape for seasonal swimming, stone-skipping, birdwatching, and traditional community riverside barbecues.

name: Khuman Lampak Main Stadium & Sports Complex
description: Sprawling across prime sports grounds in central Imphal East, the Khuman Lampak Sports Complex is the crown jewel of Manipur's legendary sports culture (celebrated across the nation as the 'Powerhouse of Sports in India'), featuring the 30,000-capacity Khuman Lampak Main Stadium, world-class indoor stadiums, boxing rings, archery ranges, swimming pools, and velodromes that have nurtured Olympic champions, world boxing champions, and football legends like Mary Kom and Mirabai Chanu.

name: Lairemba Waterfall & Foothill Stream (Wakha)
description: Hidden deep within the shaded oak and bamboo ravines of Wakha village at the western base of the Nongmaiching mountain range 9 km east of Imphal, Lairemba Waterfall is a refreshing seasonal and perennial forest cascade that plunges over mossy stone tiers into a calm, shallow natural rock basin, surrounded by wild flowering shrubs, songbirds, and quiet hiking paths frequented by local trail walkers.

name: MAASI Complex (Manipur Adventure and Allied Sports Institute)
description: Spread across 120 undulating acres at the picturesque foot of Awaching hill in Keirao about 10 km southeast of Imphal, MAASI is the Northeast's premier adventure sports institute, featuring certified natural rock-climbing cliffs, artificial bouldering walls, high-rope obstacle courses, a natural obstacle swimming pond, jungle trekking circuits, and scenic camping grounds overlooking lush valley paddies.

name: Mahabali Temple & Sacred Monkey Forest (Mahabali Umang)
description: Situated on the picturesque eastern bank of the Imphal River in Wangkhei, Mahabali Temple is an ancient brick shrine built in 1725 CE during the reign of Maharaja Garib Niwas (Pamheiba), featuring unique Bengal-style terracotta hut architecture housing a venerated stone idol of Lord Hanuman, surrounded by the Mahabali Umang—a dense, centuries-old sacred grove populated by a protected troop of revered rhesus macaque monkeys.

name: Mutua Museum & Cultural Complex Andro
description: Established in 1993 by dedicated cultural historian Mutua Bahadur in the historic village of Andro 25 km east of Imphal, Mutua Museum is an internationally celebrated living ethnographic cultural repository, featuring full-scale authentic thatch-and-timber model houses representing all 29 major ethnic tribal and Meitei communities of Manipur, traditional woodcarvings, bell-metal casting workshops, archaic coin collections, and traditional hand-coiled unglazed pottery.

name: Poiroupat Heritage Wetland & Birding Lake (Andro/Yairipok Foothills)
description: Cradled in the southern foothills of the Nongmaiching range near the Andro-Yairipok border 18 km southeast of Imphal, Poiroupat is a serene, historic natural freshwater lake and wetland covered in seasonal lotus blooms, wild water-lilies, and floating phumdi mats, steeped in ancient Meitei folkloric ballads and serving as a tranquil winter feeding habitat for migratory teals, whistling ducks, and purple moorhens.

name: Sanamahi Kiyong Temple (Nongmaiching Hill / Baruni Ching)
description: Crowning the sacred crest of Nongmaiching Hill (Baruni Ching) at an elevation of over 1,000 meters in Imphal East, Sanamahi Kiyong is a majestic, recently constructed temple complex dedicated to Lainingthou Sanamahi, the supreme ancestral creator deity of the Meitei religion (Sanamahism), designed with traditional octagonal cosmological architecture, intricately carved teak woodwork, sweeping courtyards, and awe-inspiring 360-degree views over the entire Imphal valley.

name: Sanamahi Temple Haying Khongbal (Ancient Meitei Deity)
description: Situated at Haying Khongbal in the 1st Manipur Rifles compound in Imphal East, consecrated in 1891 during the reign of Maharaja Kulachandra, this historic red-brick temple is dedicated to Lainingthou Sanamahi (the supreme creator and household guardian deity of the Sanamahi indigenous Meitei faith), renowned for its distinctive octagonal brick sanctum, tiered conical roof, and as the spiritual epicenter of the grand annual Mera Houchongba festival celebrating hill-valley solidarity.

name: Santhei Natural Park Andro
description: Nestled in the lush green foothills of the Nongmaiching hill range in Andro village 25 km east of Imphal, Santhei Natural Park is an award-winning community-managed eco-tourism park developed around a natural mountain stream reservoir, featuring manicured floral lawns, pine and eucalyptus groves, footbridges, bamboo gazebos, and picnic spaces overlooking crystal mountain water.

name: Sekta Archaeological Living Museum (Sekta Kei Excavation Mound)
description: Located along the scenic eastern bank of the Iril River approximately 16 km northeast of Imphal, Sekta Kei is a nationally renowned archaeological protected site that preserves a multi-layered prehistoric and proto-historic burial complex excavated by the Archaeological Survey of India and State Archaeology, showcasing in-situ secondary funerary urns, rare burial urn pottery, copper bangles, silver jewelry, and human remains dating from the early centuries of the Common Era.

name: Shree Krishna Temple (Brahmapur Guru Aribam Leikai)
description: Located in the historic Brahmin quarter of Brahmapur Guru Aribam Leikai along the eastern bank of the Imphal River, Shree Krishna Temple is one of the earliest standing brick monuments in Manipur, constructed in 1725 CE under the patronage of Maharaja Garib Niwas, featuring an exquisite double-roofed hut structure (Do-chala influenced) adorned with terracotta mouldings, housing ancient brass murtis of Radha and Krishna.

name: Shree Shree Govindajee Temple Imphal
description: Situated adjacent to the historic Palace Compound in Imphal East, consecrated in 1846 during the reign of Maharaja Nara Singh and rebuilt in 1891, celebrated as the highest institutional temple and spiritual nucleus of Gaudiya Vaishnavism in Manipur, renowned for its classical Hindu-Meitei temple architecture featuring twin soaring gold-plated domes, a vast paved sanctum courtyard, and magnificent carved marble and wood deities of Radha-Govinda flanked by Balarama, Krishna, Jagannatha, Subhadra, and Gaura-Nitai.

name: Silheipung Ecological Garden Lamlai
description: Situated in Lamlai 15 km east of Imphal along the highway to Ukhrul, Silheipung is a celebrated community-based eco-tourism craft park established to preserve and celebrate indigenous Manipuri craftsmanship and rural agrarian heritage, featuring landscaped botanical lawns, traditional thatched artisan workshops, water bodies, indigenous bamboo swings, an open-air amphitheatre, and live demonstrations of cane and pottery craft.

name: St. Joseph's Cathedral Imphal (Mantripukhri Cathedral)
description: Perched on a scenic, elevated hillock at Mantripukhri along National Highway 2 approximately 5 km north of central Imphal, consecrated in 1999 as the cathedral seat of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Imphal, celebrated for its monumental architecture featuring soaring curvilinear rooflines inspired by traditional tribal morung timber roofs, a magnificent high altar, stained glass windows depicting biblical scenes, and peaceful pine-shaded grounds.

name: Temple of Madan Mohanji (Palace Compound, Imphal East)
description: Erected within the historic Royal Palace Compound in Imphal East during the reign of Maharaja Chandrakirti Singh in the mid-19th century, the Temple of Madan Mohanji is a serene Vaishnavite brick shrine dedicated to Lord Krishna (Madan Mohan), noted for its distinctive rectangular sanctum, classical corbelled dome roof, ornamental stucco floral friezes, and enduring role in the grand annual Radhashtami and Raas Leela festivals of the royal court.

name: Temple of Thangal General (Wangkhei / Palace Compound)
description: Constructed in 1879 CE by General Thangal—one of the supreme military commanders and national heroes of Manipur who was executed by the British after the Anglo-Manipuri War of 1891—this historic temple at Wangkhei is an ASI and State Protected Monument, distinguished by its unique architectural fusion of indigenous Meitei conical forms and classical brick corbelled arches, housing revered Vaishnavite deities and historic dedication inscriptions.

name: Three Mothers Art Gallery (Thangapat Mapal)
description: Founded in 1986 by visionary master sculptor Gurumayum Shyamsunder Sharma at Thangapat Mapal in Palace Compound, Three Mothers Art Gallery is a world-unique wood sculpture museum named after the mother who gave birth, the motherland, and the mother tongue, housing dozens of astonishingly intricate, monumental monolithic sculptures meticulously carved from single discarded dead tree trunks and roots without any joints.

name: Bir Tikendrajit Memorial Complex & Historic Senapati Residence Grounds
description: Situated in the historic civil precinct of Imphal West adjoining Bir Tikendrajit Park and the high court area, this memorial complex marks the ancestral residence and martyrdom grounds of Jubraj Bir Tikendrajit (the Crown Prince and Senapati of Manipur) who led the gallant Manipuri resistance during the 1891 Anglo-Manipuri War, featuring a life-sized bronze equestrian monument, memorial cenotaphs, historical photo galleries, and manicured floral gardens.

name: Chorus Repertory Campus & Theatre Sanctuary (Shamushang)
description: Established in 1976 by Sangeet Natak Akademi laureate and global theatre visionary Ratan Thiyam at Shamushang Uripok in Imphal West, the Chorus Repertory Campus is a world-acclaimed theatrical sanctuary spanning two lush acres, harmoniously designed with traditional Manipuri mud-and-bamboo thatch architecture, open-air Greek-Meitei fusion amphitheatres, natural lotus ponds, and bamboo groves where indigenous theatrical masterpieces are conceived and staged.

name: Ima Keithel (Khwairamband Bazar) - Mothers' Market
description: Situated in the bustling heart of Imphal across three colossal multistoried colonial-style brick buildings (Purana Bazar, Laxmi Bazar, and New Market), established in the 16th century, celebrated globally as the largest exclusively all-women-run market in Asia and the world, where over 5,000 licensed married Meitei women traders ('Imas' or Mothers) wearing traditional Phanek and Inaphi attire independently operate stalls selling organic mountain produce, indigenous herbs, hand-woven textiles, brass utensils, and ceremonial items.

name: Imphal West Botanical Garden & Ecological Park (Langol Reserve Fringe)
description: Spread across the gentle foothill fringes of the Langol Forest Reserve near Lamphelpat, this government-maintained botanical and ecological garden is a peaceful conservation repository showcasing native flowering plants of the sub-Himalayan eastern valley, rare bamboo varieties, ornamental seasonal floral beds, paved walking circuits, and shaded benches popular with families, birdwatchers, and morning fitness enthusiasts.

name: Iroisemba Pine Hillock Trails & Nature Reserve
description: Rising directly behind the Manipur Zoological Garden on the western periphery of Imphal, the Iroisemba Pine Hillocks are an expansive network of tranquil, elevated pine ridges laced with winding dirt walking trails, fragrant conifer needles, natural bird habitats, and scenic hill vantage spots looking out over the rolling agricultural fields of the western valley toward Kangchup.

name: ISKCON Temple Imphal (Mani Mandir)
description: Situated at Airport Road in Sangaiprou approximately 4 km from central Imphal, consecrated in 1987 by ISKCON under the inspiration of Bhaktisvarupa Damodara Swami (Dr. T.D. Singh), celebrated as one of Northeast India's most architecturally unique Hindu temples, famous for its French-château-inspired white tower spires, soaring stained glass windows depicting Lord Krishna's pastimes, luminous ceiling frescoes illustrating the classical Manipuri Raas Leela, and carved marble deities of Sri Sri Radha Krishnachandra.

name: Kaboleikai War Cemetery Imphal West
description: Situated at Kaboleikai in Imphal West, this commemorative World War II memorial cemetery is maintained to honor the brave indigenous civilian porters, auxiliary scouts, guides, and medical support personnel from Manipur and the surrounding hills who rendered invaluable service to the Allied Fourteenth Army during the siege of Imphal in 1944, featuring stone memorial tablets, neat hedgerows, and tranquil lawns.

name: Kangchup Dam & Upper Canals (Scenic Foothill Vantage & Reservoir)
description: Located on the northwestern rim of Imphal West 16 km from the capital, Kangchup is a picturesque foothill vantage point and historic upland water supply reservoir established in the British era, featuring crystal-clear mountain canal feeders, stone masonry sluice gates, terraced hill gardens, pine copses, and panoramic vantage points looking down across the sprawling Imphal valley floor.

name: Kangla Fort & Royal Citadel
description: Situated on the banks of the Imphal River in central Imphal across 237.6 acres, Kangla ('dry land' in ancient Meitei) was the ancient fortified capital and spiritual power seat of the Kingdom of Manipur from the reign of King Nongda Lairen Pakhangba in 33 CE until its capture by British forces in 1891, handed back to the people of Manipur by Prime Minister Manmohan Singh in November 2004, protected as a state archaeological site featuring the monumental brick Western Gate, the twin colossal dragon-lion statues of Kangla Sha, the sacred coronation hall of Kangla Uttra, the revered Nungjeng Pukhri sacred pond, the restored Govindajee temple sanctum, and centuries-old moats.

name: Kangla Moats (Inner & Outer Royal Watercourses & Heritage Promenade)
description: Encircling the historic Kangla Fort in two concentric rings connected to the Nambul and Imphal rivers, the ancient Kangla Moats (Thangapat) were engineered centuries ago as formidable military defensive water barriers and royal dragon-boat racing channels (Hiyang Tannaba), today transformed into tranquil water courses dotted with floating white water lilies, graceful pedestrian bridges, lighted walking promenades, and traditional rowing boats.

name: Kangla Museum & Royal Artifacts Gallery (Kangla Fort Complex)
description: Housed within restored historic heritage barracks inside the sacred Kangla Fort complex in Imphal West, the Kangla Museum is an exceptional archaeological and royal repository that documents over two millennia of Manipur's royal dynastic history, displaying ancient Meitei Puyas (bark manuscripts), prehistoric polished stone celts, royal ceremonial palanquins, British-era artillery, traditional royal ceremonial weaponry, and rare archival maps of the ancient citadel.

name: Kangla Uttra & Kangla Sha Ancestral Citadel Shrines
description: Situated at the sacred geographical apex of the inner citadel of Kangla Fort, Kangla Uttra was the ceremonial royal coronation sanctum and hall of state where the Ningthous (kings) of Manipur were consecrated, flanked by the colossal reconstructed statues of the Kangla Sha—the mythical winged dragon-lion state emblem of Manipur blown up by the British in 1891 and reconstructed in 2007—and the sacred coronation stone seat.

name: Khonghampat Orchidarium
description: Sprawling across 200 acres along National Highway 2 approximately 10 km north of central Imphal, maintained by the Forest Department of Manipur, celebrated as one of Northeast India's premier orchid conservation repositories, harboring over 110 rare, endemic, and endangered orchid species including the Blue Vanda (Vanda coerulea), Dendrobium, Cymbidium, and Paphiopedilum in natural forest groves, open-air nurseries, and poly-houses.

name: Koirengei Old Airfield & Battle of Imphal Airbase
description: Situated at Koirengei 10 km north of central Imphal along National Highway 2, Koirengei Old Airfield was a critical forward operational airbase of the Royal Air Force (RAF) and Indian Air Force (IAF) during World War II, from which Spitfire and Hurricane fighter squadrons launched sorties against the advancing Japanese 15th Army during the 1944 Battle of Imphal, preserving sections of the historic wartime bitumen runway, aircraft dispersal revetments, and commemorative plaques.

name: Langthabal Royal Palace Ruins & Historic Monuments (Canchipur)
description: Crowning a picturesque, pine-crested hillock at Canchipur 6 km south of Imphal adjacent to the Manipur University campus, Langthabal is a monumental 19th-century royal palace complex founded by Maharaja Gambhir Singh in the 1820s following the Seven Years Devastation (Chahi Taret Khuntakpa), featuring atmospheric red-brick palace pavilions, ancestral royal burial chhattris (samadhis), ancient Radha-Govinda temples, aged jackfruit orchards, and panoramic outlooks across the southern valley.

name: Manipur State Museum & Art Gallery
description: Inaugurated in 1969 by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi near the historic Polo Ground in central Imphal, celebrated as the premier repository of Manipur's historical and anthropological heritage, housing comprehensive galleries covering ethnology, archaeology, natural history, textiles, and numismatics, renowned for its open-air gallery displaying the monumental 78-foot-long wooden royal dragon-headed boat 'Hiyang Hiren' (carved from a single giant tree trunk), royal portraits, medieval gold armaments, and traditional costumes of the hill tribes.

name: Manipur Zoological Garden Iroisemba
description: Situated at the foot of pine-covered hillocks at Iroisemba 6 km west of Imphal, established in 1976 across 8 hectares of natural moist deciduous forest, affectionately hailed as the 'Jewel Box' of Manipur, celebrated as a vital ex-situ breeding sanctuary for the state's state animal - the critically endangered Sangai brow-antlered deer (Rucervus eldii eldii), as well as the rare Serow (Nongin), Hoolock Gibbon, Slow Loris, Clouded Leopard, and Himalayan Black Bear.

name: Mapal Kangjeibung - World's Oldest Living Polo Ground
description: Situated in the very center of Imphal adjacent to Kangla Fort, recognized globally by sports historians and Guinness World Records as the oldest operational polo ground in the world, where the ancient indigenous sport of 'Sagol Kangjei' (traditional Meitei polo played with seven riders aside on indigenous Manipuri ponies using bamboo-root balls and cane mallets) has been played continuously since King Kangba introduced it during ancient times and formalized in 33 CE by King Nongda Lairen Pakhangba, host to the annual Manipur Polo International tournament.

name: Nambul Riverfront Promenade & Heritage Bridges (Downtown Imphal)
description: Flowing north-to-south through the center of Imphal West between the bustling commercial sectors of Thangal Bazaar and Paona Bazaar, the Nambul River is the historic water artery that sustained traditional canoe commerce and vegetable barter in royal times, now featuring newly developed riverside promenades, landscaped green river embankments, historic iron footbridges, and evening pedestrian plazas.

name: Nityapat Chuthek & Sacred Krishna Radha Shrines (Uripok)
description: Nestled in the traditional neighbourhood of Uripok along the western approaches to Kangla, Nityapat Chuthek is a historic cultural and sacred street renowned as the living cradle of classical Manipuri Vaishnavite culture, home to ancestral Krishna shrines established during the reign of Maharaja Chandrakirti Singh in the mid-19th century, hereditary Sankirtana guilds, classical Ras Leela costume ateliers, and traditional courtyard devotional performances.

name: Nungjeng Pukhri Sacred Royal Pond Kangla
description: Situated within the sacred inner sanctum of Kangla Fort in central Imphal, Nungjeng Pukhri is an ancient, rectangular sacred royal pond revered in Meitei spiritual cosmology as the primeval underwater dwelling place of Lord Pakhangba (the supreme ancestral serpent deity of Manipur), surrounded by ancient sacred trees and stone steps, historically used for royal coronation purification ceremonies and water rituals since the reign of King Nongda Lairen Pakhangba in 33 CE.

name: Nupi Lal Memorial Complex
description: Situated near the historic Polo Ground along Bir Tikendrajit Road in central Imphal, this commemorative memorial complex honors the historic Nupi Lal ('Women's War' in Meitei) movements of 1904 (against forced labor under colonial rule) and 12 December 1939 (against British rice-export policies causing local famine), featuring a magnificent larger-than-life bronze sculptural tableau depicting brave Manipuri women armed with clubs and bare hands confronting British officers and bayonets.

name: Pakhang Laiseng Sacred Shrines Kangla
description: Situated across the sacred archaeological precinct inside Kangla Fort, the Pakhang Laiseng shrines represent the most revered primeval sanctums of the Ningthouja dynasty, including the sacred Kangla Uttra (where royal oaths and coronation decrees were proclaimed), the sacred coronation stone seat 'Phambal', the Pakhangba Temple, and sacred stone altars where offerings have been made to the royal divine ancestor Lord Pakhangba for two millennia.

name: Paona Bazaar & Thangal Bazaar Heritage Commercial Corridors
description: Forming the beating commercial heart of downtown Imphal West flanking Bir Tikendrajit Road, Paona Bazaar and Thangal Bazaar are historic trade corridors established in the late 19th century, renowned across the region for authentic Manipuri Muga and Mulberry silk handlooms (Inaphi and Phanek), delicate gold-plated jewellery workshops, bronze bell-metal handicrafts, tribal cane goods, and buzzing street eateries serving authentic Singju and Bora snacks.

name: Punshilok (Langol Hills Re-Wilding Sanctuary & Spring Trails)
description: Perched along the upper slopes of the Langol hill range in Imphal West, Punshilok (meaning 'Spring of Life') is an internationally lauded 300-acre indigenous forest re-wilding sanctuary painstakingly restored from barren scrubland by local environmental crusader Moirangthem Loiya and his volunteers since 2002, featuring over 250 native tree species, perennial natural water springs, medicinal bamboo groves, birdwatching footpaths, and rustic eco-camping shelters offering sweeping valley vistas.

name: Sekmai Riverbed Picnic Shallows & Koubru Foothill Fringe (Awang Sekmai)
description: Situated in the northern reaches of Imphal West 18 km from Imphal along National Highway 2, Awang Sekmai is renowned for the crystalline mountain waters of the Sekmai River flowing over wide, clean pebble beaches and shallow gravel flats against the magnificent backdrop of the Koubru hill range, celebrated across Manipur as a premier seasonal picnic retreat, wild freshwater wading haven, and home to indigenous culinary traditions.

name: Shaheed Minar & Bir Tikendrajit Park
description: Standing majestically within the beautifully landscaped Bir Tikendrajit Park in the center of Imphal, Shaheed Minar is an imposing three-columned concrete obelisk rising against the sky, topped by the mythological three-feathered Meitei royal crest, commemorating the supreme sacrifice of Crown Prince Bir Tikendrajit, General Thangal, and countless Meitei and tribal patriots who were publicly executed on this exact spot on 13 August 1891 following the Anglo-Manipur War.

name: Shri Bijoy Govindajee Temple Sagolband
description: Situated at Sagolband on the western bank of the Nambul River in central Imphal, established in the late 18th century during the reign of King Bhagyachandra (who created the classical Manipuri Raas Leela), this revered temple enshrines the sacred idol of Bijoy Govindajee, world-famous as the historic ceremonial starting point and presiding shrine of the ancient religious royal boat race 'Heikru Hidongba' held annually on the 11th day of Langban (September) on the temple's sacred moat.

name: Yaral Pat & Lamphel Pat Wetlands Imphal
description: Situated on the fringes of Imphal city (Lamphel Pat to the west and Yaral Pat to the east), these historic wetland lakes are vital ecological and flood-moderating water bodies of the Imphal valley, celebrated for their blooming lotus flowers, aquatic food plants ('Thangjing' and 'Izing'), and serving as crucial urban wintering habitats for migratory birds including whistling teal and jacanas.

name: Ancestral Heroes Memorial Complex & Freedom Fighter Statues (Jiribam)
description: Prominently located within the municipal grounds of Jiribam, the Ancestral Heroes Memorial Complex is the foremost patriotic landmark of the western border district, featuring magnificent bronze statues and memorial pedestals dedicated to the supreme national heroes of Manipur—Bir Tikendrajit, General Thangal, Paona Brajabashi, and communist revolutionary pioneer Jana Neta Hijam Irabot—surrounded by landscaped flowerbeds and ceremonial flags.

name: Babupara & Jiri Riverfront Promenade (Jiribam Town Heart)
description: Anchoring the civic and commercial center of Jiribam town along the eastern bank of the Jiri River, Babupara is a bustling, multicultural neighborhood featuring riverside promenades, bustling morning fish markets laden with fresh catch from the Barak and Jiri rivers, traditional bamboo and cane handicraft cooperatives, and lively local eateries serving authentic spicy fish curry and steamed rice cakes.

name: Barak River Islands & Wetland Sandbars (Western Riverine Wilderness)
description: Stretching along the broad, meandering course of the Barak River as it navigates the western lowlands of Jiribam, these expansive seasonal sand islands (chars), braided river channels, and marshy riverine wetlands form a pristine winter ecosystem that attracts thousands of migratory wild ducks, purple moorhens, kingfishers, and river terns, creating a peaceful wilderness haven for avid birdwatchers and landscape photographers.

name: Jiri River Pebble Beds & Heritage Suspension Crossings
description: Flowing gently along the historic boundary dividing Manipur from Assam's Cachar district, the Jiri River features scenic bends with wide, smooth river pebble beds, calm emerald-green waters shaded by towering bamboo and teak trees, and historic pedestrian suspension footbridges swaying gently above the water, providing picturesque border vistas and peaceful waterside recreation.

name: Jiri-Makru Wildlife Sanctuary & Rainforest Corridor Jiribam
description: Sprawling across 198 square kilometers in the western hill ranges of Jiribam and Tamenglong districts along the Jiri and Makru river basins, Jiri-Makru Wildlife Sanctuary is celebrated as one of Manipur's richest primary tropical rainforest reserves, characterized by dense semi-evergreen and bamboo jungles, clear river channels, and serving as a vital sanctuary for Hoolock Gibbons, Spotted Linshangs, Clouded Leopards, Hornbills, and wild elephants.

name: Jiribam Railway Station & Western Gateway Railhead Heritage
description: Inaugurated in 1990 as the historic first railway terminus in the state of Manipur, Jiribam Railway Station marks the state's western gateway to the Indian Railways network, set amidst scenic rolling green hills and tea gardens, featuring broad-gauge platforms, charming British-influenced railway architecture, local tea stalls serving spiced chai, and a historic diesel locomotive siding.

name: Jiri–Barak River Confluence (Jirimukh Scenic Estuary)
description: Situated at the southern tip of the district where the fast-flowing Jiri River empties into the colossal Barak River, Jirimukh is a magnificent natural water junction characterized by sweeping gravel bars, expansive white sand spits, deep swirling river pools inhabited by golden Mahseer and river catfishes, and panoramic views of the forested hills of southern Assam and western Manipur.

name: Leishabithol Waterfalls & Natural Forest Cascades (Sonapur)
description: Hidden deep within the lush sub-tropical evergreen foothills of Sonapur village 8 km southeast of Jiribam town, Leishabithol Waterfall is a secluded natural cascade that tumbles down multiple tiered sedimentary sandstone shelves into cool, crystal-clear rock basins, enclosed by thick stands of wild banana, bamboo, and blooming jungle orchids that create a peaceful haven for local nature trekkers.

name: Ningshing Khun Biodiversity Park & Memorial Complex Jiribam
description: Situated at Ningshing Khun in the western plains of Jiribam district bordering southern Assam, explicitly featured in the official Tourism Department portal as a designated tourist destination, comprising an extensive ecological biodiversity park preserving indigenous flora, botanical nurseries, landscaped walking promenades, and an imposing memorial complex honoring historical regional pioneers and martyrs who developed the western river frontier.

name: Old Cachar-Manipur Royal Highway Trails (Historic Cachar Road)
description: Winding through the dense sub-tropical bamboo and oak forests of the western hills of Jiribam, the Old Cachar Road (historically known in part as Tongjei Maril) is an ancient royal bridle path that for centuries served as the lifeline corridor connecting the Meitei royal kingdom in Imphal with the Cachar plains and British Bengal, featuring mossy stone trail cuts, historic rest-house clearings, and colonial telegraph line remnants.

name: Ramgaizang Village & Western Manipur Foothill Trails
description: Nestled against the emerald eastern slopes of the Western Manipur hill range 6 km east of Jiribam town, Ramgaizang is a tranquil indigenous Rongmei Naga village celebrated for its sprawling hillside orchards of organic pineapples, cashews, and oranges, traditional timber-and-thatch houses, crystal clear mountain streams, and elevated hiking trails offering breathtaking panoramas across the Barak-Jiri plains.

name: Angaan Ching Eco Park & Sunrise Hill (Kakching)
description: Crowning a prominent hill ridge on the eastern outskirts of Kakching town, Angaan Ching Eco Park is an inspirational community-led ecological sanctuary and reforested green hill, developed through mass volunteer tree planting to restore indigenous flora, featuring paved walking trails, medicinal plant gardens, an ancient hillside Shiv Mandir (Mahadev Temple), a children's park, and sweeping 360-degree panoramic viewpoints overlooking the southern Manipur valley.

name: Kakching Garden
description: Nestled amidst the rolling hills and dense forests of Manipur, the Kakching Garden is a serene trekking paradise. Located within a 30-acre forest area, this picturesque haven beckons nature enthusiasts, adventure-seekers, and birdwatchers alike to explore its unspoiled beauty. The garden boasts an impressive collection of indigenous trees, plants, and wildflowers, making it a haven for botanists, bird enthusiasts, and wildlife photographers.

name: Kakching Khunou & Hilltop Viewpoint
description: Perched on a scenic, elevated undulating landscape in southern Kakching district 55 km from Imphal, Kakching Khunou is a historic agrarian settlement celebrated for its tranquil rural lifestyle, terraced paddy fields, ancient sacred groves dedicated to Umang Lai deities, and the elevated Kakching Khunou Ching hilltop viewpoint that commands magnificent panoramic vistas of Pumlen Lake and the surrounding hills.

name: Kakching WWII Aerodrome Remains (Allied Airfield Plains)
description: Spreading across wide, flat open grasslands on the southern edge of Kakching town, the Kakching Aerodrome is an important historic Allied airfield constructed during World War II in 1943-1944 to support Royal Air Force and US Army Air Forces fighter squadrons defending Imphal and launching sorties into Japanese-occupied Burma, today preserving grassy runway foundations, aircraft dispersals, and open horizons popular for evening walks and kite-flying.

name: Kharung Pat & Northern Kakching Wetland Basin
description: Situated in the northern floodplains of Kakching district near Wabagai and Keirak, Kharung Pat is an expansive natural freshwater lake basin fed by the Sekmai and Thoubal river channels, featuring extensive shallow water zones, submerged aquatic flora, floating vegetation mats, and quiet reed beds that provide vital nesting grounds for local water hens, teals, and kingfishers.

name: Lamjao Pat & Wetland Marshlands (Khoidum-Mayeng Lamjao)
description: Tucked between the southern rim of Pumlen Lake and the agricultural hamlets of Mayeng Lamjao and Khoidum Lamjao, Lamjao Pat is a serene, pristine freshwater wetland marsh characterized by lush floating biomass islands (phumdis), blooming white water-lilies, tall reed beds, and winding canoe channels where local fishermen navigate traditional wooden dugouts to harvest native fish and lotus stems.

name: Lousi Pat & Ngangou Pat Freshwater Wetlands
description: Lying in the fertile lowland basin southwest of Kakching Khunou, Lousi Pat and Ngangou Pat are historic freshwater lakes and wetland depressions celebrated in regional lore for ancient indigenous irrigation engineering and drainage canals dug in royal times, today supporting rich aquatic biodiversity, sprawling wild water-lily blossoms, traditional cast-net fishing, and abundant waterbirds.

name: Pallel Border Trade Foothill Town
description: Situated at the picturesque base of the eastern hills 45 km southeast of Imphal along National Highway 102, Pallel is a vibrant commercial transit junction marking the physical boundary where the flat Imphal valley ends and the steep mountain ascent to Tengnoupal and Moreh begins, celebrated for its bustling multi-ethnic bazaar selling organic mountain pineapples, king chillies, fresh mountain ginger, and traditional bamboo baskets.

name: Pallel Foothill Riverbeds & Maring-Chothe Border Market
description: Situated at the strategic gateway where the flat Kakching valley ascends dramatically into the forested Chandel hill ranges, Pallel is a vibrant border market town and geographic crossroads along the Indo-Myanmar highway, featuring rocky riverbed strolls along the Palel stream, vibrant morning markets where Maring, Chothe, and Meitei communities exchange hill produce, wild honey, and seasonal fruits, and panoramic views of the ascending mountain ridges.

name: Pumlen Pat Lake & Floating Island Wetland
description: Situated in southern Kakching district adjacent to Kakching Khunou 50 km south of Imphal, Pumlen Pat is the second-largest natural freshwater lake in the state of Manipur after Loktak Lake, spanning over 22 square kilometers of open water, interconnected floating biomass phumdis, and rich aquatic flora, celebrated by conservationists as a potential secondary translocation habitat for the endangered Sangai brow-antlered deer and a vital winter sanctuary for thousands of migratory waterfowl.

name: Sekmai River Promenade & Riverbank Picnic Shallows (Kakching)
description: Flowing past the eastern outskirts of Kakching town below the slopes of Uyok Ching, the Sekmai River creates picturesque sweeping bends characterized by clean rounded river pebbles, crystal-clear wading shallows, and lush shaded bamboo groves that provide the premier natural riverside recreation and family picnic grounds for the town's residents during the dry winter season.

name: Serou Historic Mahaprabhu Temple & Riverfront
description: Serou Historic Mahaprabhu Temple & Riverfront is an authentic attraction destination located in ,  district of Manipur. Celebrated for its regional significance and unique ambiance, it offers travelers an immersive experience in the culture, scenic beauty, and heritage of Manipur.

name: Sugnu Frontier Town & Manipur River Gorge
