description: Situated at the southern tip of the Imphal valley 65 km south of Imphal along the confluence of Kakching, Chandel, and Churachandpur districts, Sugnu is an ancient historic trading town celebrated for its dramatic geographical location where the wide meandering Manipur River dramatically narrows and carves a roaring gorge through the southern hills, featuring scenic riverside walking promenades, traditional Meitei fishing communities, and sweeping views of the southern mountain ranges.

name: Thongjao & Chairel Traditional Red-Clay Pottery Hamlets
description: Situated along the rich alluvial riverbanks of the Sekmai and Arong rivers, Thongjao and Chairel are historic craft villages renowned across Manipur for their centuries-old red-clay pottery tradition, where skilled women artisans craft cooking pots, storage jars, ritual vessels, and flower pots entirely by hand without a potter's wheel, utilizing indigenous wooden paddles, anvils, and open-air straw firings.

name: Tummu Ching Heritage Tourism Centre Hiyanglam
description: Perched atop a sacred green hillock at Hiyanglam in Kakching district 45 km south of Imphal, Tummu Ching is a designated heritage tourism destination developed by the Tourism Department, Government of Manipur, celebrated in local Meitei folklore as the sacred seat of ancient clan deities, featuring a newly constructed heritage pavilion, panoramic observation decks overlooking the sprawling paddy fields of Kakching and the Thoubal River, and extensive native tree afforestation.

name: Uyok Ching Forest Trail & Statue of Hao Sampubi
description: Stretching along the elevated forested ridge directly behind the manicured lawns of Kakching Garden, Uyok Ching is a sacred forest hill steeped in deep Meitei folklore, home to the revered open-air shrine and tragic memorial statue of Hao Sampubi (a celebrated heroine of folklore), ancient Pakhangba ritual spots, natural oak and teak groves, and shaded dirt trails looking out over the winding Sekmai River.

name: Waikhong Valley & Organic Pineapple Orchards
description: Nestled in the gentle foothill amphitheatre of southern Kakching 10 km south of the district headquarters, Waikhong is a picturesque agrarian settlement famed across Manipur for producing some of the sweetest organic Queen and Kew pineapples, sprawling across undulating red-soil hill slopes alongside smallholder tea gardens, traditional handloom weaving households, and clear stream-side walking tracks.

name: Wangoo Lampak & Ancient Meitei Sacred Sites
description: Situated along the scenic banks of the Manipur River in southern Kakching district 60 km from Imphal, Wangoo (comprising Wangoo Lampak and Wangoo Terakhong) is an ancient Meitei settlement renowned for its deep historical antiquity, celebrated in state archaeology for ancient stone inscriptions, traditional potters who create unglazed earthen water pots, and as the host venue of traditional Meitei boat races and the annual sacred river rituals of Wangoo Ahallup.

name: Ango Ching Virgin Rainforest Wilderness Kamjong
description: Sprawling across approximately 150 square kilometers of rugged, virtually inaccessible mountain ridges in Kamjong district along the international boundary with Myanmar, Ango Ching is celebrated as one of Manipur's last remaining primary virgin rainforest wildernesses, characterized by dense multi-tiered subtropical semi-evergreen canopies, crystal mountain torrents, and serving as a crucial trans-boundary wildlife corridor harboring wild Asian Elephants, Tigers, Clouded Leopards, Hoolock Gibbons, Gaur, and Great Hornbills.

name: Chammu Historic Frontier Sub-Base & WWII Defence Ridge
description: Perched on a strategic mountain ridge just 5 km from the international border with Myanmar, Chammu is a historic frontier village steeped in ancient Tangkhul spirit lore as the gateway to the sacred Kazeiram realm, preserving overgrown World War II British 14th Army defensive bunkers, weapons pits, and patrol pathways from 1944 when Allied forces guarded the high mountain passes against Japanese incursions.

name: Chatric Khullen Heritage Village & Indo-Myanmar Border Ridge
description: Perched on a scenic, fog-wrapped mountain ridge in southeastern Kamjong directly overlooking the Myanmar border, Chatric Khullen is an ancient Tangkhul heritage settlement that preserves traditional timber-and-slate village architecture adorned with wood-carved hornbill and buffalo head motifs, extensive hillside terraces producing world-renowned organic Chatric ginger, and ancient community gathering megaliths.

name: Kamjong Town Hilltop & Luira-Mangkhap Cultural Grounds
description: Perched gracefully along an elevated mountain saddle over 1,500 meters high, Kamjong town serves as the administrative capital of the district, featuring traditional Tangkhul wooden homesteads with carved gables, panoramic viewing platforms overlooking deep forested valleys, and the central community festival grounds where the ancient agricultural festivals of Luira Phanit (seed-sowing) and Mangkhap Phanit (post-transplantation thanksgiving) are celebrated with traditional folk dancing, wrestling, and feasts.

name: Kasom Khullen & Phungyar Tangkhul Highlands
description: Perched on undulating forested mountain ridges in southern Kamjong district 50 km from Ukhrul, Kasom Khullen and Phungyar form the cultural heartland of the southern Tangkhul Nagas, celebrated for their rich traditions of polyphonic choral folk singing, ancient stone feast-of-merit monoliths, sweeping vistas of the Mapithel mountain range, and traditional terraced ginger and passion-fruit cultivation.

name: Kazei Kharalung & Mythological Stone Sharpening Relics (Kazei Hills)
description: Perched among the mist-shrouded oak forests of the Kazei hills in eastern Kamjong, Kazei Kharalung is an ancient natural and legendary megalithic geological site officially celebrated by the district administration, revered in Tangkhul Naga mythology as the sacred sharpening stone where ancestral warriors and wandering spirits of the afterlife hone their spectral dao swords and spears before entering the netherworld.

name: Kazeiram Spirit Sanctuary & Kazei Keirak (Ancestral Stone Ladder)
description: Situated in the secluded mountain wilderness of eastern Kamjong, Kazeiram (meaning 'Land of the Dead' in Tangkhul) is the most sacred cosmological landscape of the Tangkhul Nagas, believed to be the spirit realm where souls depart after mortal life, accessed via Kazei Keirak—an extraordinary natural staircase of non-man-made tiered stone steps carved into the mountain ridge, venerated as the mystical ladder between the mortal earth and the spirit universe.

name: Khayang Waterfalls (Khayang Falls)
description: Hidden deep in the pristine forested valleys of the Indo-Myanmar frontier near Khayang village in Kamjong district 65 km from Ukhrul town, Khayang Waterfalls is celebrated as one of the highest and most majestic plunge waterfalls in Manipur, where a roaring mountain torrent drops over 100 meters (330 feet) in an unbroken white ribbon down dark granite cliffs into a deep, crystal-clear sapphire basin surrounded by virgin bamboo and fern rainforests.

name: Kongou Waterfall & Primary Rainforest Canyon
description: Carving a dramatic limestone defile in the Sahamphung forest tract of central Kamjong, Kongou Waterfall is a towering, isolated mountain fall cascading over dark, mossy rock steps into a deep, misty canyon, shrouded in ancient primary sub-tropical evergreen rainforest where rare hornbills, barking deer, and wild orchids flourish in an undisturbed wilderness.

name: Liabi Waterfall & Chatric-Siyang Forest Gorge
description: Hidden deep within the pristine sub-tropical mountain forests between Chatric and Siyang villages in southeastern Kamjong near the Myanmar frontier, Liabi Waterfall is an officially recognized natural spectacle where a ferocious mountain torrent drops over a sheer vertical precipice into a secluded, emerald-green plunge basin, surrounded by giant jungle ferns, wild orchids, and towering hardwood trees untouched by modern logging.

name: Mapithel Dam (Thoubal Multipurpose Reservoir Chadong)
description: Constructed across the Yangwui Kong (Thoubal River) at Phayang and Chadong in Kamjong district 35 km east of Imphal, Mapithel Dam (Thoubal Multipurpose Project) features an imposing 66-meter-high earthen dam that has created an immense, breathtaking sapphire-blue water reservoir nestled between the green forested spurs of the Mapithel mountain range, becoming one of Manipur's premier scenic lake destinations for recreational motorboating, speedboating, and waterside camping.

name: Ningthi Village & Chamu River Angling Shallows
description: Situated in a verdant mountain valley along the pristine banks of the Chamu (Sanalok) River in eastern Kamjong, Ningthi is an idyllic Tangkhul tribal village renowned for its crystal-clear river shallows flowing over polished white gravel bars, traditional cane-and-wire hanging suspension bridges swaying above the water, organic orange groves, and peaceful riverbed camping sites famous for indigenous angling.

name: Nungourok Cliff Viewpoint & Cloud Inversion Promontory
description: Jutting out dramatically over deep forested river gorges in eastern Kamjong at an elevation exceeding 1,600 meters, Nungourok Cliff is an exhilarating mountain promontory renowned among local trekkers for its jaw-dropping sunrise views, where a vast sea of white billowy clouds completely submerges the valleys below, creating the sensation of standing above an endless white ocean extending toward the hills of Myanmar.

name: Phikoh & Grehang Easternmost Border Outposts
description: Situated at the absolute eastern geographic limits of Manipur where motorable roads terminate against the international frontier with Myanmar, Phikoh and Grehang are remote frontier outposts featuring historic international boundary pillars, mountain ridge trails traversed by traditional trans-border trade, and breathtaking views of the vast Yu and Chindwin river basins rolling across the Burmese borderlands.

name: Ramrei Eco Park & Chadong Reservoir Backwater Gazebos
description: Nestled along the eastern shores of the Mapithel Dam reservoir at Ramrei village in western Kamjong about 30 km east of Imphal, Ramrei Eco Park is a breathtaking lakeside recreation haven featuring emerald-green backwaters winding like Scandinavian fjords between rolling mountain spurs, traditional bamboo picnic gazebos built over water, country boat landings, local food huts serving fried lake fish, and camping grounds.

name: Kalapahar Grasslands & Rolling Meadows (NH-2 Ridge)
description: Stretching along the elevated mountain ridges overlooking National Highway 2 between Kangpokpi and Senapati, Kalapahar is a picturesque high-altitude countryside haven celebrated for its undulating, emerald-green rolling meadows, grazing cattle herds, traditional Gorkha dairy settlements, fresh dairy tea kiosks, and breezy vantage points looking down across the misty Sadar Hills valley.

name: Kangpokpi Town & Saddle Mountain Range
description: Situated along National Highway 2 (Imphal-Dimapur Highway) 45 km north of Imphal, Kangpokpi (Kpi) is the scenic administrative headquarters of Kangpokpi district, situated in a picturesque river basin surrounded by the soaring peaks of the Koubru and Sadar Hills ranges, renowned for its cool mountain climate, historic Christian mission institutions founded in 1919, expansive organic vegetable markets, and sweeping vistas of the surrounding mountain spine.

name: Keithelmanbi Riverbanks & Pebble Shallows
description: Meandering past the historic settlement of Keithelmanbi along the valley floor between the Koubru and Sadar Hills ranges, this scenic mountain river stretch features wide, clean river pebble beds, calm crystal-clear pools, and bamboo-shaded riverbanks that provide a peaceful riverside escape for weekend family outings, shallow-water wading, and stone-skipping.

name: Leikop & Daili Hill Ridges (Cloud-Inversion Highway)
description: Perched along the high mountain spine connecting Kangpokpi to the northern frontier ranges, Leikop and Daili are picturesque hill-crest hamlets renowned among highway travelers for their dramatic vantage points, where early-morning winter temperatures produce vast sea-of-clouds inversions filling the deep river valleys below, with only mountain summits protruding like green islands above the mist.

name: Mount Koubru (Sacred Koubru Peak) & Range
description: Rising majestically to an altitude of 2,562 meters (8,405 feet) north of the Imphal valley in Kangpokpi district, Mount Koubru is celebrated in Meitei mythology as the sacred primeval mountain where human civilization first originated ('Awang Koubru Asuppa'), revered as the dwelling place of Lord Koubru (one of the nine primordial gods of the Meitei pantheon), featuring an ancient rock cave shrine on the wind-swept summit plateau, wild bamboo meadows, and panoramic views spanning the entire Imphal valley.

name: Sadu Chiru Waterfall (Leimaram Falls)
description: Nestled in the lush, densely forested foothills of the Koubru mountain range near Sadu Chiru and Leimaram villages 29 km southwest of Imphal, celebrated as one of Manipur's most iconic and visited natural waterfalls, where a roaring mountain stream plunges over three cascading rock shelves into a deep natural stone plunge pool below, surrounded by wild banana groves, fern-covered cliffs, and timber resting gazebos.

name: Sahmuleno Waterfall & Forest Plunge Pool
description: Nestled in a secluded jungle ravine in the western hills of Kangpokpi, Sahmuleno Waterfall is an enchanting natural forest cascade that pours over mossy sandstone ledges into a deep, crystal-clear wading pool, surrounded by thick stands of wild ginger, elephant ferns, and shaded by sub-tropical canopy that creates a refreshing, peaceful sanctuary for village trail trekkers.

name: Saikul Valley & Iril River Headwaters
description: Nestled in an expansive, picturesque mountain basin in eastern Kangpokpi 28 km from Kangpokpi town, Saikul Valley is a tranquil agrarian haven where the nascent headwaters of the Iril River flow between rolling green hills, fertile terraced rice paddies, traditional timber-and-bamboo Kuki homesteads, and charming suspension hanging footbridges spanning the gentle river currents.

name: Singda Dam & Forest Reservoir
description: Situated in the pine-covered foothills of the Koubru range 16 km northwest of Imphal at an altitude of 920 meters, Singda Dam is recognized as the highest mud (earthen-core rockfill) dam in the world, built across the Singda River, creating an expansive, tranquil emerald-blue mountain lake surrounded by dense evergreen deciduous hills, featuring an elevated observation tower, landscaped picnic lawns, and cool mountain breezes.

name: Taphou Waterfalls & Forest Cascades (Taphou Kuki)
description: Hidden deep within the lush sub-tropical oak and pine forests of Taphou Kuki village about 6 km south of Kangpokpi town, Taphou Waterfalls is an officially celebrated natural attraction comprising a magnificent sequence of three distinct cascading waterfalls that plunge over moss-carpeted granite shelves into deep, crystal-clear rock basins, enclosed by towering tree ferns, wild orchids, and tranquil village walking tracks.

name: Thangal Surung Eco-Park & General Thangal Birthplace
description: Located at Thangal Surung in the scenic Sadar Hills about 15 km from Kangpokpi town, this eco-park and heritage site preserves the ancestral birthplace of General Thangal—the revered national hero and supreme military commander of Manipur executed by the British after the 1891 Anglo-Manipuri War—featuring a natural limestone cavern (Surung), a memorial cenotaph, traditional Thangal Naga cultural artifacts, and landscaped hillside viewpoints.

name: Thangthupimol View Point & Sadar Hills Promontory (Kontam)
description: Rising high above the valley near Kontam village in southern Kangpokpi, Thangthupimol View Point is an elevated mountain promontory offering jaw-dropping 360-degree panoramic vistas across the entire Sadar Hills basin, where rolling mountain ranges, terraced hill villages, and the meandering river valley unfold beneath sweeping skies.

name: Twilhakol (Twilshakol) Waterfall (IT Road / Chalwa)
description: Plummeting over 500 feet in an awe-inspiring, roaring white sheet from towering vertical cliffs near Chalwa village along the interior IT Road (Imphal-Tamenglong Road) in western Kangpokpi, Twilhakol (Twilshakol) Waterfall is one of the highest and most spectacular hidden cascades in Manipur, crashing into a colossal spray-shrouded limestone gorge surrounded by virgin bamboo and sub-tropical broadleaf jungle.

name: Zaimeng Lake & High-Altitude Wetland (Thonglang Ridge)
description: Perched at an altitude of over 2,100 meters atop the Thonglang mountain ridge in northern Kangpokpi, Zaimeng Lake (meaning 'Lake of No Return' or 'Mystery Lake' in Liangmai Naga) is a mystical high-altitude natural freshwater body and bog surrounded by dense dwarf bamboo brakes, wild rhododendrons, rare mountain herbs, and perpetual swirling mist, revered in local tribal legends as a sacred enchanted sanctuary.

name: Haochong Valley & Organic Mandarin Orange Orchards
description: Tucked into a sun-drenched, tranquil mountain basin in northern Noney 25 km from the district headquarters, Haochong is an idyllic Rongmei Naga sub-divisional hill valley celebrated across the state for its sprawling hillside orchards of sweet, organic Khasi mandarin oranges, traditional stilt timber homes, clear mountain streams with natural wading pools, and festive orange harvest celebrations.

name: Irang River Shallows & Suspension Footbridges (Nungba)
description: Winding through a colossal forested canyon in the Nungba sub-division of central Noney along NH-37, the Irang River is one of the principal natural waterways of western Manipur, characterized by broad white sandbars, turquoise mountain shallows flowing over smooth boulders, deep natural fishing holes, and classic swaying cable suspension footbridges connecting remote Rongmei cliff hamlets to the main highway.

name: Khoupum Valley & Khoupum Dam Lake
description: Nestled in a lush, emerald intermontane valley basin enclosed by forested mountain walls in Noney district 80 km west of Imphal, Khoupum is an idyllic cultural valley of the Rongmei Naga tribe, renowned for its thousands of acres of lush green paddy fields, traditional stilt bamboo houses, vibrant Ga-Ngai post-harvest festival celebrations, and the massive Khoupum Dam built across the Machangduan River creating an expansive sapphire lake ideal for boating and angling.

name: Khoupum Waterfall (Pristine Forest Cascade)
description: Hidden deep in the dense semi-evergreen forests near Khoupum village in Noney district, celebrated in the 2014 and 2022 Manipur Tourism Policies as a designated adventure tourism asset, where a rushing mountain stream plunges over steep volcanic rock formations into a deep, crystal-clear natural plunge pool surrounded by dense wild bamboo groves and lush ferns.

name: Khukdai Cave & Geological Rock Shelters (Khoupum)
description: Concealed beneath towering limestone crags and dense evergreen canopy in the forested hills flanking the Khoupum valley, Khukdai Cave is an ancient natural limestone cavern and rock shelter steeped in centuries of Rongmei Naga folklore, featuring narrow stalactite chambers, subterranean dripping freshwater springs, and historic rock alcoves historically used by ancestral tribal warriors and village elders for ritual offerings and strategic refuge.

name: Leimatak River Gorge & Western Mountain Vista
description: Carving a colossal, near-vertical chasm between the southern mountain ridges of Noney and Churachandpur, the Leimatak River gorge is one of the most rugged and visually striking river corridors in Manipur, featuring roaring turquoise rapids, sheer granite cliffs draped in climbing lianas and moss, and elevated mountain lookout points offering breathtaking views into the deep abyss below.

name: Makru River Canyon & Virgin Rainforest Valley (Western Noney)
description: Flowing through an untamed, deep mountain defile along the western border of Noney district, the Makru River is celebrated as one of the cleanest and wildest mountain rivers in Manipur, carving dramatic vertical cliff gorges draped in virgin bamboo and hardwood forests, featuring turquoise deep-water pools teeming with native golden Mahseer fish, white pebble beaches, and historic highway bridge crossings.

name: Noney (Longmai) Bridge Canyon & Ijai Riverbed Rapids
description: Carved deep into the mountain bedrock at Longmai (Noney town), this dramatic natural canyon where the Ijai (Eji) River rushes over giant water-worn granite boulders forms the dramatic natural foundation above which the world-record 141-meter-tall Noney Railway Bridge soars, featuring riverside hiking trails along rocky rapids, natural swimming pools, and awe-inspiring upward angles gazing at the colossal concrete piers rising into the sky.

name: Noney Railway Pier Bridge Viewpoint
description: Situated across the deep, misty Ijai (Eji) River gorge in Noney district 63 km west of Imphal, constructed by Northeast Frontier Railway as the flagship engineering marvel of the Jiribam-Imphal railway line, world-famous for Bridge No. 164 which features a monumental pier rising to a staggering height of 141 meters (462 feet), officially recognized as the tallest railway pier bridge in the world (surpassing Europe's 139-meter Mala Rijeka Viaduct in Montenegro).

name: Old Cachar Bridle Trails & Heritage Trade Route (Noney Sector)
description: Traversing the rugged mountain ridges of Noney district along the historic Tongjei Maril corridor, the Old Cachar Road bridle trail is an ancient trade and communication artery cut through dense sub-tropical rainforests, historically utilized by royal Meitei expeditions, British colonial armies, and pack-mule caravans, featuring surviving dry-stone embankment walls, hand-cut stone steps, and iron colonial mile markers.

name: Taodaijang & Satudai Traditional Rongmei Weaving Hamlets
description: Nestled in the quiet foothills near Khoupum in Noney district, Taodaijang and Satudai are historic Rongmei Naga villages celebrated as the heartland of traditional backstrap loin-loom weaving, where generations of skilled craftswomen hand-weave iconic ethnic textiles including the Pheisuai (traditional wrap skirt with striking red, black, and white bands) and Mareipan (warrior shawl) using organic hand-spun cotton and natural plant dyes.

name: Thangagong Peak & Khoupum Valley Panorama
description: Rising steeply above the eastern rim of the emerald Khoupum valley basin to an elevation exceeding 1,800 meters, Thangagong Peak is the premier high-altitude trekking summit in southern Noney, requiring an invigorating ridge climb through pine copses and rhododendron groves that rewards adventurers with a jaw-dropping bird's-eye view across the entire 15-km flat expanse of Khoupum valley, its sparkling dam, and the distant Barak river gorges.

name: Tupul Integrated Tourist Destination & Eco-Tourism Complex
description: Perched on a scenic, breeze-swept mountain plateau at Tupul along National Highway 37 in eastern Noney about 50 km west of Imphal, Tupul Integrated Tourist Destination is a designated state eco-tourism hub developed by Manipur Tourism, featuring landscaped terraced gardens, traditional wooden cottages, scenic viewing pavilions looking onto the monumental railway viaducts of the Jiribam-Imphal project, and nature trails through sub-tropical pine and oak woodlands.

name: Bungkhawpui Bat Caves & Barak River Bluffs
description: Carved into the colossal limestone cliffs flanking the eastern banks of the mighty Barak River near Bungkhawpui village, these natural subterranean caverns and rocky bluffs form a dramatic geological landscape home to thousands of native insectivorous bats, featuring natural stalactite fissures, hidden river lookout alcoves, and wild hiking trails overlooking the turquoise river gorge.

name: Hringtuinek (Sartuinek) Stream & Wilderness Ravines
description: Deep in the remote southern wilderness of Pherzawl near the border with Mizoram, the Hringtuinek (Sartuinek) stream is an untouched mountain tributary that cuts a dramatic course through sheer rocky ravines and virgin sub-tropical rainforest, featuring crystal-clear cold rapids rushing over granite shelves, natural rock wading basins, and shaded sandbars that provide pure wilderness solitude.

name: Luipi Waterfall & Natural Plunge Pool (Pherzawl Corridor)
description: Located along the scenic highway corridor approximately 28 km outside Pherzawl town in southern Manipur, Luipi Waterfall is an officially recognized natural attraction where a torrential mountain brook plunges over sheer, mossy rock shelves into a deep, crystal-clear jade-green plunge pool, surrounded by dense sub-tropical evergreen rainforest, towering wild bamboo, and giant ferns.

name: Parbung Highland Town & Mountain Viewpoints
description: Perched at an altitude of over 1,200 meters on a prominent mountain crest in the Tipaimukh sub-division of southern Pherzawl, Parbung is a scenic highland hill town that commands breathtaking 360-degree vistas of the southern mountain chains, featuring pine-fringed walking tracks, traditional Hmar wooden cottages with flower-filled verandas, and lively hill markets offering organic mountain honey, dried fish, and indigenous handlooms.

name: Pherzawl Old Village Site & Chief Bulhmang Heritage Memorial
description: Situated in the historic settlement core of Pherzawl town at Muolveng, this heritage site preserves the ancestral village foundations of the Hmar chieftaincy, featuring the revered stone tomb of Chief Pu Bulhmang (the celebrated founding chief of Pherzawl), ancient clan memorial megaliths, traditional timber-and-slate village architecture, and the historic grounds of Pherzawl High School established in 1951 as one of the earliest high schools in the southern hills.

name: Saidan & Muolveng Traditional Hmar Cultural Hamlets
description: Nestled in the rolling forested hills adjoining Pherzawl town, Saidan and Muolveng are historic Hmar tribal hamlets celebrated for preserving indigenous cultural heritage, including intricate backstrap loin-loom weaving of traditional Hmar puan shawls (such as the Hmaram, Ngotekherh, and Thangsuo Puan), traditional timber-and-bamboo house architecture, ancestral stone memorials, and vibrant folk music traditions.

name: Senvawn Tlang & Historic 1910 Christian Heritage Ridge
description: Perched on a scenic, wind-swept mountain ridge in southern Pherzawl overlooking the international borderlands and the deep river valleys into Mizoram, Senvawn is revered as the spiritual and educational cradle of Christianity in southern Manipur, established when local Hmar chiefs welcomed Welsh pioneer missionary Watkin Roberts in 1910, featuring historic stone mission churches, memorial centenary monuments, and breathtaking cloud-inversion panoramas.

name: Thanlon Highland Town & Vangai Mountain Ridge Pherzawl
description: Perched atop an elevated, wind-swept mountain ridge in northern Pherzawl district 95 km from Churachandpur at an altitude of 1,400 meters, Thanlon is an atmospheric sub-divisional hill station of the Paite and Hmar tribes, renowned for its cool alpine climate, sweeping vistas of the mist-draped Vangai mountain range, ancient tribal memorial stones, traditional wood-and-tin hillside dwellings, and organic ginger farming.

name: Tipaimukh Confluence of Tuivai and Barak Rivers Pherzawl
description: Situated at the tri-junction of Manipur, Mizoram, and Assam in Pherzawl district 180 km from Imphal, Tipaimukh ('Mouth of the Tuivai River') is celebrated as one of the most spectacular natural river confluences in Northeast India, where the rushing, turquoise-blue Tuivai River from Mizoram merges with the mighty Barak River flowing from Manipur, carving a colossal, dramatic canyon between towering rainforest-covered mountain walls.

name: Tuipi River Rapids & Forest Gorge
description: Rushing through an inaccessible mountain defile in central Pherzawl, the Tuipi River is a scenic mountain river tributary of the Barak characterized by roaring white-water rapids, small sparkling cascades, dramatic limestone rock shelves, and dense riverine bamboo forests that create an unspoiled natural sanctuary for adventurous river trekkers and nature explorers.

name: Tuivai Riverbed Shallows & Border Angling Rapids
description: Flowing along the deep southern boundary separating Pherzawl district from northeastern Mizoram, the Tuivai River is celebrated for its pristine, unpolluted waters characterized by turquoise pools, bubbling rocky rapids, and wide white pebble beaches, enclosed by towering jungle-draped cliffs that offer world-class catch-and-release angling for golden Mahseer and idyllic wild riverside camping.

name: Vangai Mountain Range & Rainforest Cloud Trails
description: Spanning the western spine of Pherzawl district overlooking the Barak River basin, the Vangai Range is an untamed, heavily forested mountain wilderness characterized by razor-sharp ridgelines, dense sub-tropical bamboo and teak forests, dramatic cloud-inversion mountain passes, and remote agricultural hamlets famous across the state for producing organic King Chilli, sweet oranges, and aromatic ginger.

name: Barak Festival Grounds Senapati
description: Situated along the scenic riverbanks of the upper Senapati and Barak river confluence near Senapati town, this dedicated festival complex is the official permanent venue for the grand state-level Barak River Festival (Barak Youth and Cultural Festival), celebrated annually every December to promote environmental conservation of the river basin, featuring inter-tribal cultural dances, traditional wrestling competitions, indigenous archery, rock concerts, and ethnic food stalls.

name: Chorei Waterfall & Forest Stream Ravine
description: Tucked away in the rugged mountain forests connecting the northern border subdivisions of Senapati, Chorei Waterfall is a secluded natural cascade where unpolluted hill streams tumble down multiple granite tiers into a shaded emerald basin. Framed by wild banana groves, towering bamboo clusters, and mossy canyon rocks, the spot provides an untouched wilderness retreat along the less-trodden forest footpaths of the northern border hills.

name: Douze Eco-Tourism Park & Ngaipai Ngaipao Waterfall (Phuba Khuman)
description: Perched on an elevated mountain ridge above Phuba Khuman village in eastern Senapati, Douze Eco-Tourism Park is a community-developed scenic plateau renowned for sweeping 360-degree panoramas of morning cloud inversions rolling over the Poumai Naga highlands. Adjacent to the park through dense subtropical pine and oak groves lies the breathtaking Ngaipai Ngaipao Waterfall (Ngaipai-Ngaipou-Siibu), where a torrential mountain brook cascades through sheer moss-draped granite rock defiles into deep, crystalline plunge pools.

name: Dzuko Valley (Manipur Sector) & Mount Iso (Tenipu)
description: Situated in northern Senapati district along the interstate border with Nagaland, Mount Iso (locally known as Tenipu) rises majestically to an altitude of 2,994 meters (9,823 feet), celebrated as the highest mountain summit in Manipur, presiding over the southern expanse of the legendary Dzuko Valley, renowned for its rolling emerald cushions of dwarf bamboo, meandering crystal mountain streams, deep gorges, and the rare endemic pink Dzuko Lily (Lilium chitrangadae) that blooms in June-July.

name: Haolaipai Supao Keikulu Cave Senapati
description: Situated in the rugged limestone hills of Senapati district near Supao and Haolaipai villages, celebrated by speleologists and adventure enthusiasts as one of northern Manipur's most intriguing subterranean karst cave systems, featuring deep natural limestone galleries adorned with glistening calcified stalactites and stalagmites, subterranean streams, and historical associations with tribal shelter during ancient warfare.

name: Koide Ancient Heritage Village & Poumai Cultural Monoliths
description: Koide is an ancient Poumai Naga ancestral hill settlement perched on a prominent spur in eastern Senapati, renowned as one of the pivotal historical villages in northern Manipur. The village preserves centuries-old stone megalithic monuments, ancestral village gateways, traditional wood-shingle huts decorated with hornbill motifs, and customary Morung dormitories where oral histories, traditional crafts, and indigenous clan councils have been maintained for generations.

name: Koubru Laikha Sacred Shiva Temple & Foothill Pilgrimage Precinct
description: Situated beside the picturesque, gushing waters of the Imphal River along the NH-2 highway corridor at Koubru Laikha, this ancient and highly revered Hindu temple complex is dedicated to Lord Shiva. Set at the scenic base of the sacred Koubru mountain range, the temple serves as a peaceful spiritual shrine for travelers on the national highway and transforms into a massive pilgrimage destination during the annual Maha Shivratri festival when thousands of devotees gather for sacred rituals and river baths.

name: Liyai Ancient Stone Pools & Sacred Banyan Grove
description: Located within the ancient mountain settlement of Liyai Khullen, this sacred cultural precinct contains the historic Male and Female stone-lined water pools carved over five centuries ago by village founders. Shaded by colossal centuries-old sacred banyan trees and traditional Morung dormitories, the crystal-clear natural spring pools are steeped in Poumai lore as the ceremonial bathing and purification grounds of ancient village warriors, located close to the legendary source springs of the Barak River.

name: Liyai Khullen & Source of the Barak River
description: Perched at a lofty altitude of 1,800 meters in northern Senapati district near the border with Nagaland 45 km from Senapati town, Liyai Khullen is an ancient Poumai Naga settlement revered as a mother village, internationally significant as the geographical source where the mighty Barak River (the second largest river system in Northeast India after the Brahmaputra) originates from a natural mountain spring trickling beneath sacred moss-covered rocks before gathering strength across valleys.

name: Makhel Farewell Monolith & Tri-Monolith Heritage Grounds
description: Located in the sacred historical village of Makhel near the NH-2 highway corridor, this revered heritage precinct encompasses the legendary stone monuments of Naga mythological migration, including the historic Farewell Monolith, the celebrated Tri-Monolith (symbolizing the ancient parting of three brothers: the Meiteis, Nagas, and Kuki-Chins), the Hailstorm Stone, and the Lucky Stone. According to ancient folklore, Makhel served as the central dispersal ground from where ancestral groups branched across Northeast India.

name: Makhel Sacred Dispersion Tree (Chutebu)
description: Situated on a scenic mountain saddle 10 km south of Mao along National Highway 2 in Senapati district, Makhel is celebrated in pan-Naga oral history as the sacred mythological point of dispersion from which major Naga tribes (Mao, Maram, Poumai, Angami, Chakhesang, Rengma, Lotha) migrated into their respective hill lands, home to the sacred banyan tree 'Chutebu' (believed to have sprouted from the walking stick of the common Naga ancestor), the sacred stone megalith 'Dispersal Stone', and the ancient parting stone.

name: Mao Border Hill Station & Cherry Blossoms
description: Perched on a windy mountain ridge at an elevation of 1,788 meters (5,866 feet) along National Highway 2 on the interstate border with Nagaland 45 km north of Senapati, Mao (Mao Gate) is celebrated as the scenic northern gateway to Manipur, famous for its cold bracing climate, vibrant organic vegetable markets, and the spectacular annual Cherry Blossom Festival in November when thousands of wild Himalayan cherry blossom trees (Prunus cerasoides) burst into pink bloom across the hill slopes.

name: Maram Khullen Megalithic Feast Courtyard & Customary Assembly Grounds
description: Perched on a strategic mountain saddle in the historic ancestral village of Maram Khullen, this ceremonial megalithic courtyard is the traditional assembly ground of the hereditary Maram royal king (Sagong). It features upright menhirs and dolmens erected during ancient Feast of Merit ceremonies, stone-lined seating circles for clan elders, and centuries-old wooden royal residences adorned with hornbill carvings, representing one of the finest living examples of traditional customary Naga governance.

name: Maram Khullen Traditional Royal Village
description: Perched on a high rocky mountain ridge 25 km north of Senapati along the road to Willong, Maram Khullen is celebrated as the ancient ancestral mother village and royal capital of the Maram Naga tribe, famous for retaining its traditional hereditary royal institution (the Sagong / King and Queen of Maram), ancient wood-carved royal dormitories decorated with mithun horns and human heads, sacred stone monoliths, and the traditional post-harvest Kanghi festival.

name: Moulkholum Hilltop Viewpoint (S. Mongbung Viewpoint)
description: Rising prominently on the hillcrest above S. Mongbung village overlooking the Senapati district headquarters and the meandering valley of the upper Senapati river, Moulkholum is an emerging natural viewpoint celebrated for panoramic vistas. Visitors can gaze across layered mountain ridges stretching toward the Nagaland border, watch spectacular morning mist rolling through deep gorges, and enjoy refreshing sub-Himalayan breezes.

name: Oinam Hill Traditional Pottery & Terraced Village
description: Perched dramatically on the steep, misty mountain spurs of the Poumai highlands, Oinam Hill village is famed across the region for its rare, indigenous coiled earthenware pottery tradition crafted exclusively by village women without a potter's wheel. Using locally sourced black clay mixed with serpentinite stone powder, artisans hand-shape durable black cooking pots and ritual urns that are prized throughout Manipur and Nagaland, set against a stunning backdrop of terraced potato, cabbage, and paddy fields.

name: Paomata Cultural Heartland & Terraced Hills Senapati
description: Perched across rolling high-altitude mountain ridges in eastern Senapati district 35 km from Senapati town, Paomata (comprising Tungjoy, Liyai, and Phaibung) is the ancestral cultural heartland of the Poumai Naga community, celebrated for its monumental stone megalithic platforms, centuries-old bachelor morungs decorated with carved wooden human and hornbill motifs, dramatic amphitheatres of stepped irrigated rice terraces, and handloom shawls.

name: Phuba Thapham Stone Monoliths & Terraces
description: Perched on a high windy mountain promontory in the Poumai tribal heartland of eastern Senapati district 35 km from Senapati town, Phuba (comprising Phuba Thapham and Phuba Khuman) is an ancient settlement celebrated for its monumental stone megaliths and stone-paved community platforms, traditional wooden morungs with horned gables, cascading irrigated terrace rice fields that wrap around mountain shoulders, and ancient village war drums.

name: Purul Heritage Village & Paoki Wrestling Grounds
description: Situated in a scenic mountain basin in eastern Senapati district 20 km from Senapati town, Purul (comprising Purul Akutpa and Purul Atongba) is a historic Poumai Naga village celebrated for its ancient martial heritage, famous for the traditional Paoki (Poumai wrestling) and Toutii festivals celebrated annually where village champions engage in intense traditional belt wrestling on grassy arenas, stone clan monuments, and intricate handloom weaving.

name: Senapati
description: The Senapati district in Manipur is a hidden gem for adventure seekers and nature enthusiasts. The area boasts pristine and scenic hills, crystal-clear lakes, and dense forests that are home to a diverse range of flora and fauna. Visitors can engage in a variety of outdoor activities, including trekking, camping, rock climbing, and bird watching, amidst breathtaking scenery. With its rich cultural heritage and pristine natural environment, Senapati presents an unparalleled opportunity to connect with Mother Nature and experience the beauty of eastern Manipur. The district is dotted with several villages, each with its unique cultural identity, offering a glimpse into the traditional lifestyle of the locals. Visitors can experience the warm hospitality of the local people, taste their unique cuisine, and participate in local festivals and events, making Senapati an unforgettable destination for those seeking an authentic travel experience in the heart of Manipur.

name: Tadubi Highland Town & Maram Hills Senapati
description: Perched on a windy mountain saddle at an altitude of 1,600 meters along National Highway 2 in northern Senapati district 30 km north of Senapati town, Tadubi is an atmospheric hill station surrounded by pine-covered peaks, serving as the strategic gateway junction for traveling into the ancient megalithic sites of Willong Khullen and the source of the Barak River at Liyai Khullen, famous for fresh organic mountain apples, pears, and traditional Mao and Maram handicrafts.

name: Tunggam Heritage Village & Ancestral Poumai Monoliths
description: Settled on high mountain saddles in the Paomata subdivision of Senapati, Tunggam is an ancestral Poumai Naga village characterized by dramatic stone megaliths, sacred clan meeting courtyards, and well-preserved timber homes with pitched thatch roofs. The village maintains deep-rooted traditional customs, age-old stone fencing, and historical oral tales associated with the legendary early dispersion of the Naga communities from Makhel.

name: Willong Khullen Megalithic Monolith Avenue
description: Situated on a windswept mountain knoll in Willong Khullen village 37 km from Maram along the Maram-Peren road, celebrated by archaeologists and historians as the 'Stonehenge of Manipur', featuring an extraordinary avenue of approximately 135 to 150 colossal standing stone monoliths (menhirs) erected in two parallel rows stretching across the grassy ridge, with several stones towering up to 7 meters (23 feet) in height, erected in prehistoric times by Maram Naga warriors to commemorate great military feats and feasts of merit.

name: Yangkhullen Ancient Stone Village
description: Perched precariously on the sheer, near-vertical rocky cliff face of a towering mountain spur 85 km from Senapati town, Yangkhullen is an extraordinary ancient tribal settlement of the Zeme Naga tribe, affectionately hailed as the 'Hanging Village of Manipur', where centuries-old stone-and-timber houses are tiered dramatically one above another on stone platforms chiseled into the rock, preserving ancient bachelor morungs, sacred stone monoliths, and untouched customary laws.

name: Akhui Range & Virgin Biodiversity Forest
description: Spanning the central mountain spine of Tamenglong west of the town, the Akhui Range is a majestic, heavily forested mountain wilderness characterized by razorback ridgelines, dense sub-tropical cloud forests, hanging epiphytic orchids, and rare endemic wildlife including the clouded leopard and serow. The range offers pristine high-elevation trekking corridors with sweeping views across both the Barak and Makru river valleys.

name: Alangtakhou Waterfall & Subterranean River Cave
description: Situated in the rugged hills of the Tamei subdivision of northeastern Tamenglong, Alangtakhou Waterfall is a geological marvel where a roaring mountain river plunges over a sheer rock cliff and rushes directly into subterranean limestone fissures and cavernous chambers before re-emerging downstream. The surrounding forest is rich in wild ginger, giant ferns, and colorful butterflies, creating an enchanting environment for adventure seekers.

name: Barak Waterfalls (Seven Cascades of the Barak River)
description: Situated in the rugged jungle canyons where the Barak River carves through steep limestone mountains in Tamenglong district, celebrated as one of Northeast India's most extraordinary fluvial spectacles, featuring a continuous series of seven magnificent roaring waterfalls cascading one after another over gigantic basalt boulders into deep natural plunge pools, highlighted in the state tourism policy as a premier destination for river rafting, kayaking, and wild river trekking.

name: Buning Meadow (Piulong) & Alpine Orchid Slopes
description: Perched on high mountain ridges in Tamei sub-division of Tamenglong district 45 km from Tamenglong town, Buning (locally known as Piulong) is an extraordinary rolling alpine grassland plateau, celebrated for its unique undulating topography composed of hundreds of gentle, rounded natural earth mounds carpeted in lush green grass, blooming wild orchids, lily species, and clear babbling brooks.

name: Chiuluan & Inriangluang Reangaans (Ancient Stone Forts & Skywalk)
description: Perched strategically on steep village boundaries in Chiuluan and Inriangluang overlooking the roaring Barak River gorge, the Reangaans are ancient megalithic stone fortifications and defensive sentry platforms built centuries ago by Rongmei warriors to safeguard ancestral village domains. Recently enhanced with community skywalk viewpoints, the site combines remarkable tribal military heritage with dizzying vertical vistas plunging into the Barak canyon.

name: Dailong Sacred Grove & Biodiversity Heritage Site
description: Situated 8 km north of Tamenglong town, Dailong is an ancient Rongmei Naga village celebrated globally for its community-conserved sacred forest grove ('Raengaan'), officially declared in May 2017 as Manipur's first Biodiversity Heritage Site under the Biological Diversity Act 2002, where the village council has protected centuries-old virgin forests, colossal ancient mahogany and fig trees, rare orchids, medicinal herbs, and sacred spirit stones without cutting a single leaf for generations.

name: Gadai Hills & Prayer Mountain Summit
description: Perched prominently on the eastern heights overlooking Tamenglong town, Gadai Hills—widely known locally as Prayer Mountain—is an elevated sacred summit blanketed in wild alpine grasses, subtropical orchids, and pine copses. The viewpoint is renowned for delivering sweeping 360-degree panoramas of the morning sea of clouds filling the deep Barak river basin and the endless undulating ridges of the western Manipur highlands.

name: Haipou Jadonang Memorial Park & Freedom Fighter Heritage
description: Situated in the town center of Tamenglong, Haipou Jadonang Memorial Park is the premier civic and historical landmark of the district, dedicated to Haipou Jadonang, the revered spiritual leader and freedom fighter who founded the Heraka movement and led an armed socio-religious uprising against British colonial rule before his martyrdom in 1931. The park features a towering bronze statue of Jadonang, landscaped flower gardens, and stone commemorative inscriptions.

name: Khoupanglang Rock Shelters & Waterfall Cave
description: Hidden within the dense subtropical jungle along the Farmlane stream corridor near Tamenglong, Khoupanglang Caves is an extraordinary multi-room natural limestone rock shelter where a perennial mountain cascade plunges directly over the cavern roof into a natural rocky pool. Visitors can stand dry inside the cavern chambers while looking out through a veil of falling water into the lush green rainforest canopy beyond.

name: Kisha Khou (Mount Kisha & Gaidinliu Cave Cliffs)
description: Rising majestically with near-vertical granite cliffs in northern Tamenglong, Mount Kisha Khou is an officially recognized tourist site revered both for dramatic geological grandeur and monumental anti-colonial history. The rugged mountain crags and concealed cliff caves served as the legendary guerrilla hideout and spiritual sanctuary for Rani Gaidinliu and her Zeliangrong freedom fighters during their armed resistance against British colonial rule in the 1930s.

name: Magulong Ancient Rongmei Heritage Village & Caves
description: Situated in the remote, densely forested mountain ridges of northern Tamenglong district near Tamei, Magulong is an ancient Rongmei Naga settlement affectionately known among speleologists as the 'Village of Caves', renowned for having over 20 natural subterranean limestone caves and rock shelters scattered across its surrounding karst hills, alongside ancient megaliths, traditional log drums, and untouched tribal customary life.

name: Nroutamphang Waterfall & Dailong Forest Gorge
description: Tucked away in the sacred virgin forest canopy of Dailong—declared Manipur's first Biodiversity Heritage Site—Nroutamphang Waterfall is an unpolluted multi-tier natural cascade tumbling down sheer moss-covered rock steps into deep jade-green swimming basins. Enclosed by towering ancient trees, wild ginger blooms, and rare epiphytic orchids, the waterfall exemplifies the pristine natural ecology preserved by community conservation rules.

name: Tamenglong
description: Tamenglong, situated in the westernmost part of Manipur, is a region of breathtaking beauty with its lush forests, rolling hills, and sparkling waterfalls. The district is home to the Barak River and its tributaries, which have carved out valleys and gorges, providing ample opportunities for trekking, rock climbing, and camping. The rich cultural heritage of the district is evident in its traditional villages, where the Zeliangrong and Kabui tribes reside, preserving their unique customs and traditions. As a trekking destination, Tamenglong offers a diverse range of experiences, from easy day hikes to challenging multi-day expeditions, catering to adventure seekers of all levels.

name: Tharon Cave (Ancient 655-Meter Limestone Cave)
description: Situated 27 km north of Tamenglong town near Tharon village, celebrated in Indian speleology and prehistory as Manipur's most extensive natural limestone cave system, measuring approximately 655.6 meters in total explored length with 34 interconnecting chambers, natural stone arches, five distinct surface exits, and engraved stone carvings that archaeologists link to the prehistoric Hoabinhian culture of Southeast Asia.

name: Tousem & Haochong Remote Rainforest Ridges
description: Perched on rugged mountain ridges in far western Tamenglong district bordering Assam along the Makru and Barak river basins, Tousem and Haochong represent one of Manipur's wildest and most remote sub-divisions, celebrated as the premier producer of the prized sweet Tamenglong Mandarin Orange (which holds the GI tag), celebrated host of the annual State Level Orange Festival in December, surrounded by roaring river rapids, suspension bridges, and virgin rainforests.

name: Tuilut Waterfall & Wilderness Rapids
description: Flowing through an inaccessible mountain valley in southern Tamenglong, Tuilut Waterfall is a spectacular perennial cascade where torrential hill waters crash over broad granite steps into foaming rapids and broad pebbled sandbars. Enclosed by dense bamboo brakes, wild fig trees, and towering cane thickets, the site offers an idyllic setting for intrepid wilderness hikers seeking untouched river defiles.

name: Zeilad Lake & Zeilad Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Nestled on a high forested plateau near the Barak River in western Tamenglong district, Zeilad is the largest of a cluster of seven sacred natural mountain lakes (including Guiphop Zei and Napshei Zei) surrounded by 85.4 square kilometers of pristine subtropical rainforest gazetted as the Zeilad Wildlife Sanctuary, revered in Rongmei Naga mythology as a sacred spirit realm, celebrated as an internationally important wintering sanctuary for migratory waterfowl, tortoises, pythons, and Great Hornbills.

name: Zeiladzang Village & Primary Hornbill Rainforest
description: Settled on pristine riverbanks in the rugged Tousem subdivision of western Tamenglong, Zeiladzang is an officially recognized tourist site surrounded by virgin primary rainforest. Accessible via adventurous jungle footpaths, the village offers a glimpse into completely off-grid tribal life, home to dense nesting populations of Great Indian Hornbills, wild orchids, and traditional timber stilt houses framed by crystalline mountain streams.

name: Bro Waterfall & Forest Stream Tengnoupal
description: Situated in the dense teak and wild bamboo forests of Tengnoupal district along the road connecting Tengnoupal to Moreh, Bro Waterfall is celebrated in the official tourism inventory as an enchanting natural water body, where a perennial hill stream cascades over stepped granite boulders into a cool natural rock pool surrounded by lush tropical flora, popular as a refreshing highway transit stop for travelers.

name: Chahmol & Sita Village Highland Foot-Trails
description: Perched along an elevated mountain spine in eastern Tengnoupal, Chahmol and Sita are remote hillside settlements encircled by native pine groves, wild mountain orchids, and scenic winding foot trails. The ridge crest commands magnificent sunrise views over early morning fog inversions that blanket the border river valleys rolling towards Myanmar.

name: Indo-Myanmar Friendship Gate & Border Crossing (Moreh)
description: Situated at the terminus of Asian Highway 1 in Moreh, the Indo-Myanmar Friendship Gate and Friendship Bridge mark the sovereign international land border connecting India with Tamu in the Sagaing Region of Myanmar. Flanked by border security outposts, international milestone markers, and the Namphalong market precinct across the bridge, this landmark crossing serves as the cultural and commercial gateway linking South Asia to Southeast Asia.

name: Khudei Khunou & Khunbi Ridge Viewpoints
description: Located along high-altitude mountain saddles in southern Tengnoupal, Khudei Khunou and Khunbi are picturesque traditional agrarian settlements inhabited by the Maring and Kuki communities. The villages are distinguished by traditional elevated timber granaries, hand-hewn wooden cottages with flowering gardens, terraced hillside maize and ginger farms, and panoramic ridge lookouts over mist-shrouded border valleys.

name: Khudengthabi Border Ridge Viewpoint & Kabaw Valley Lookout
description: Perched on a prominent mountain saddle along the NH-102 descent toward Moreh, Khudengthabi is a renowned high-altitude viewpoint that marks one of the most dramatic geological transitions in Manipur. Looking eastward from the ridge, visitors are rewarded with breathtaking vistas of endless subtropical rainforests stretching out into Myanmar's vast, sunlit Kabaw Valley and the distant mountain ranges of Sagaing.

name: Kwarok Tampak Stream Trails & Sandstone Pools
description: Winding through a secluded foothill valley below the Tengnoupal ridges, Kwarok Tampak is an unpolluted wilderness corridor characterized by gentle stream fords, natural sculpted sandstone pools, and towering sub-tropical evergreen tree canopies. The trail is famed locally for its soothing natural ambience, chirping cicadas, colorful forest butterflies, and seasonal wading pools.

name: Kwatha Village (Indo-Myanmar Organic Bamboo Shoot Settlement)
description: Nestled in an isolated, lush jungle valley 16 km north of Moreh near the international border, Kwatha is a unique cultural marvel: it is the only Meitei-inhabited village situated entirely in the southern hill tracts of Manipur, preserving centuries-old traditional mud-and-thatch architecture, ancient ancestral customs, and globally famed as the culinary epicenter of authentic organic fermented bamboo shoots ('Kwatha Soibum'), produced using traditional underground anaerobic fermentation pits fed by mountain spring water.

name: Langol Peak Garden (Tlanglhungbung Leikol) & WWII Camp
description: Perched at an elevation of over 1,500 meters along a soaring mountain ridge in the Machi hill tract, Langol Peak Garden (locally known as Tlanglhungbung Leikol) is the premier ecotourism destination of the region, featuring landscaped hillside floral gardens, wooden viewing pavilions, sweeping 360-degree vistas across the Indo-Myanmar border hills and the Kakching plains, ancient folklore connections to the epic Khamba-Thoibi legends, and historic trench remnants from World War II Allied operational encampments during the Battle of Imphal.

name: Lokchao River Gorges & Crystal Shallows
description: Cutting through the dense teak, bamboo, and dipterocarp rainforests within the buffer zones of the Yangoupokpi-Lokchao sanctuary, the Lokchao River is celebrated for its crystal-clear emerald waters rushing over smooth white boulders and pebbled sandbars. Shaded by towering tropical canopies that host diverse hornbills, flying squirrels, and wild orchids, the riverbed provides idyllic natural swimming pools and secluded forest riverside trails.

name: Lokchao Wildlife Sanctuary Moreh
description: Sprawling across 184.8 square kilometers of rugged hills and dense semi-evergreen and moist deciduous forests along the international boundary with Myanmar near Moreh, established in 1989, Yangoupokpi Lokchao Wildlife Sanctuary is celebrated as a critical component of the Indo-Burma Global Biodiversity Hotspot, harboring rare trans-boundary wildlife including the Malayan Sun Bear, Slow Loris, Serow, Sambar, Clouded Leopard, Pangolin, and over 150 species of tropical forest birds.

name: Machi Sacred Groves & Northern Ridge Sanctuaries
description: Perched on the northern mountain ridges of Tengnoupal, the sacred forest groves of Machi have been protected for centuries under strict customary Maring tribal taboos. Towering ancient trees, wild ficus, and sacred standing stones within these groves are revered as ancestral spiritual abodes, preserving unique pockets of virgin biodiversity, native medicinal plants, and traditional tribal animist lore.

name: Moreh Border Bazaar & International Trade Precinct
description: Located in the bustling commercial heart of Moreh border town, this vibrant international border bazaar is celebrated across Northeast India as an exotic shopping haven. The bazaar overflows with authentic Myanmar goods, including traditional Thanaka cosmetic paste, jade and ruby jewelry, Burmese teak carvings, woven lungis, Chinese electronics, exotic dry fruits, and multicultural borderland street food blending Meitei, Kuki, Tamil, and Burmese culinary influences.

name: Moreh Border Town
description: Moreh Border Town, situated in the Chandel district of Manipur, is a thriving village that has been a significant trade hub between India and Myanmar. With its unique blend of Indian and Southeast Asian cultures, Moreh offers an enchanting experience for visitors. The town's proximity to the international border has created a fascinating melting pot of traditions, languages, and cuisines. The stunning natural surroundings, including rolling hills, lush forests, and sparkling waterfalls, provide a perfect backdrop for trekking, bird watching, and nature walks. As the sun sets, the town comes alive with the sounds of local markets and the aroma of exotic delicacies, making Moreh Border Town an unforgettable destination for travelers. The town's strategic location also offers opportunities for cross-border interactions and a glimpse into the rich history of the region, with the nearby town of Tamu in Myanmar being an important cultural and trade center.

name: Shenam Pass (Scraggy Peak & WWII Battle Saddle)
description: Perched dramatically along the winding heights of NH-102 across the Tengnoupal hills, Shenam Pass (often celebrated historically as the Scraggy Peak saddle) is a formidable mountain gorge famous for sheer rock cliffs, whistling wind corridors, and sea-of-clouds panoramas. In 1944, this strategic pass was the epicenter of relentless combat between British-Indian forces and the Imperial Japanese Army during the Battle of Imphal, where allied soldiers defended the razorback ridges guarding the gateway into the Imphal valley.

name: Suvaikenu Lim & Tuilong Vadung Cascades
description: Tucked away in the rugged mountain ravines of interior Tengnoupal along ancient foot trails, Suvaikenu Lim and Tuilong Vadung form a pristine sequence of natural forest waterfalls and crystal-clear plunge pools. Rushing through dense wild banana thickets, bamboo groves, and ancient mossy sandstone boulders, the cascades offer an unspoiled nature retreat where local tribal villagers have waded and fished for generations.

name: Tengnoupal Mountain Peak & Strategic Ridge
description: Perched on a windy mountain ridge 70 km from Imphal along National Highway 102, Tengnoupal is celebrated as the highest point on the entire Indo-Myanmar Road at an elevation of 1,450 meters (4,757 feet), offering dramatic panoramic vistas over the vast Kabaw Valley of Myanmar to the east and the Manipur valley to the west, celebrated in World War II history as the fiercely contested mountain pass where Allied forces held off the Japanese 33rd Division in 1944.

name: Athokpam Anglo-Manipur War Site & Historical Landmark
description: Located at Athokpam Awang in the northern suburbs of Thoubal town along the historic military road, this commemorated heritage site marks a pivotal defensive battleground where Manipuri soldiers valiantly engaged advancing British forces during the decisive Anglo-Manipur War of April 1891. The site preserves a stone memorial obelisk, commemorative historical plaques, and shaded memorial grounds honoring the regional patriots who sacrificed their lives.

name: Charangpat Fishermen Canals & Freshwater Locks
description: Charangpat is an interconnected wetland landscape featuring traditional wooden canal locks, stone weirs, and freshwater waterways that link the seasonal lake basins of Ikop and Kharung. Lined by swaying bamboo clusters, rustic bamboo footbridges, and floating phumdi vegetation, the canals offer a vivid window into the age-old indigenous fishing techniques and waterway transportation of the Meitei lake dwellers.

name: Ikop Pat & Kharungpat Freshwater Lakes
description: Situated in the central eastern alluvial plains of Thoubal district 30 km south of Imphal, Ikop Pat and adjacent Kharungpat form one of Manipur's most significant natural wetland lake complexes, spanning over 13 square kilometers of open water, floating reed beds, and marshlands, celebrated as a crucial wintering refuge for thousands of migratory waterfowl from northern Asia including Lesser Whistling Ducks, Ferruginous Pochards, and Bar-headed Geese.

name: Kaina Hill & Sacred Govindajee Jackfruit Tree Sanctuary
description: Rising to an altitude of 921 meters amidst lush green teak and pine groves at Yairipok 29 km southeast of Imphal, Kaina is celebrated in Manipuri Gaudiya Vaishnavism as a sacred holy hillock, where in the 18th century Maharaja Bhagyachandra had a divine vision of Lord Govindajee directing him to carve the sacred deities of Shree Govindajee from a colossal jackfruit tree growing on this exact hill, featuring a historic hilltop temple, sacred tree shrines, and tranquil forested walking paths.

name: Khangabok Traditional Pottery & Sericulture Village
description: Khangabok is an expansive traditional rural settlement celebrated across the state as a thriving hub of indigenous craftsmanship. Village lanes are alive with master potters hand-shaping utilitarian clay pots, decorative urns, and cooking vessels on traditional wheels, alongside sericulture cottages where silkworm rearing, silk reeling, and handloom weaving of fine Manipuri silk shawls have been practiced for generations.

name: Khongjom War Memorial & Kheba Hill
description: Situated on the historic slopes of Kheba Hill along National Highway 102 (Indo-Myanmar Road) 36 km south of Imphal, Khongjom is revered across India as the sacred battleground of the last battle of the Anglo-Manipur War fought on 23-25 April 1891, where Major Paona Brajabasi and his brave Meitei warriors fought to the death against overwhelming British forces rather than surrender, featuring an imposing 30-foot white marble sword monument, a grand memorial gate, a war museum, and an artificial musical lake.

name: MMRC & Unity Park (Khangabok)
description: Located along NH-102 at Khangabok in Thoubal district, the Manipur Mountaineering and Trekking Association (MMTA)-associated MMRC & Unity Park is a sprawling recreational and educational cultural park dedicated to national integration and Meitei heritage. The park features life-sized traditional Meitei thatched houses (Yumjao), an artificial lake with recreational paddle boating, ethnic handicraft exhibition pavilions, children's adventure rides, and lush botanical gardens displaying regional medicinal flora.

name: People's Museum (Thoubal Town)
description: Located in Thoubal town, the People's Museum is an understated yet invaluable community-curated cultural institution preserving thousands of rare anthropological artifacts from Manipur's varied ethnic communities. The collections include ancient copper-plate inscriptions, traditional palm-leaf manuscripts (Puya), antique musical instruments, royal loin-loom textiles, indigenous agricultural tools, and martial weapons dating back centuries.

name: Phouoibi Park & Harvest Goddess Memorial (Charangpat)
description: Situated at Charangpat Maning in central Thoubal, Phouoibi Park is a serene community eco-park dedicated to Lady Phouoibi, the revered Meitei deity of paddy, agricultural prosperity, and fertility. The landscaped park features green lawns, decorative water fountains, commemorative statues depicting ancient agricultural folklore, paved walking tracks, and flowering groves overlooking the surrounding agricultural plains of Thoubal.

name: Salungpham Green Hills & Citrus Orchards
description: Nestled at the base of the eastern hill range along the outer perimeter of the Thoubal valley, Salungpham is a picturesque rural hamlet surrounded by rolling green hillocks, betel nut groves, and terraced citrus orchards. The village serves as a tranquil rural eco-tourism destination with shaded walking trails leading up to scenic ridge viewpoints overlooking the entire central Manipur valley basin.

name: Shri Bungshibudon Temple & Sacred Meitei Heritage Precinct
description: Officially recognized by Manipur Tourism, Shri Bungshibudon Temple is a historic religious and cultural shrine dedicated to the ancestral guardian deity Bungshibudon. Surrounded by an ancient sacred grove of banyan and peepal trees in Thoubal, the temple complex serves as the traditional venue for vibrant annual Lai Haraoba ceremonies featuring ritual dances, oral chanting, and customary Meitei animist offerings.

name: Tentha Pink Lotus Wetlands & Waterway Canals
description: Stretching across the low-lying agricultural plains of southern Thoubal, the Tentha wetlands form a tranquil network of freshwater canals, marsh channels, and natural ponds. During late summer and autumn, vast stretches of these waterways are blanketed in dazzling displays of pink and white Nelumbo lotus blooms, attracting birdwatchers, native wetland fishers in wooden dugout canoes, and landscape photographers.

name: Thamlai Waterfall & Hill Forest Stream
description: Hidden within the picturesque eastern foothill forests of Thoubal near Thamlai village, Thamlai Waterfall is a pristine natural cascade where clear mountain waters plunge over stepped rock shelves into a refreshing jade-green rock basin. Shaded by dense subtropical bamboo groves, wild fig trees, and flowering shrubs, the waterfall provides an idyllic offbeat nature sanctuary for adventurous hikers seeking solitude.

name: Thoubal River Promenade & Town Waterfront
description: Originating in the forested hills of Ukhrul district and flowing through the heart of Thoubal town before joining the Imphal River at Irong, the Thoubal River is celebrated as the primary geographical and economic lifeline of eastern Manipur valley, featuring newly developed riverside promenades with paved pedestrian walkways, ornamental streetlights, landscaped tree plantings, and scenic footbridges in central Thoubal town.

name: Waithou Lake & Waithoupat Wetland
description: Nestled against rolling green hillocks along National Highway 102 just 16 km south of Imphal, Waithou Lake (Waithoupat) is a picturesque freshwater lake and wetland ecosystem, celebrated for its expansive beds of blooming pink lotuses, water lilies, migratory waterfowl, and the historic roadside village of Waithou world-famous across Manipur for its mouthwatering traditional smoked freshwater fish ('Nga Atoiba' and 'Ngamu') prepared over smoldering paddy husks.

name: Duncan Ecological Park (Ukhrul Town)
description: Nestled on a scenic forested spur on the outskirts of Ukhrul town, Duncan Ecological Park is an officially documented public eco-park and botanical recreational sanctuary. Enclosed by fragrant native Khasi pine groves, the park features landscaped floral terraces, shaded wooden gazebos, stone pathways, and open green lawns that serve as a favorite weekend picnic destination for families and travelers.

name: El Shadai Eco-Park & Pine Grove Picnic Sanctuary
description: Perched on a serene hillock overlooking the surrounding pine valleys on the periphery of Ukhrul town, El Shadai Eco-Park is an officially recognized community recreation park. Shaded by dense stands of tall evergreen pine trees, the park features rustic wooden seating pavilions, floral garden plots, family picnic spaces, and scenic viewpoints offering panoramic vistas of morning valley mists.

name: Hundung Mova Cave & Lungshang River Gorge (Hungpung)
description: Featured officially on the Ukhrul District Administration's dedicated tourist places portal, Hundung Mova Cave (also known as Mova Limestone Cave) is an ancient geological cavern formation located near Hungpung / Hundung. The cavern opens into a colossal natural limestone hall capable of sheltering over a hundred people simultaneously, featuring ancient calcified rock draperies, natural skylight fissures, and an adjoining gorge where the crystal-clear Lungshang River rushes over smooth limestone boulders.

name: Jessami Frontier Village & WWII Battle Ridge
description: Perched on a strategic mountain promontory overlooking the confluence of the Lanye and Thetsu rivers in far northern Ukhrul district along the border with Nagaland 115 km from Ukhrul town, Jessami is celebrated in World War II military history as the site of the legendary Battle of Jessami fought on 28 March - 1 April 1944 where the 1st Battalion of the newly raised Assam Regiment made their heroic first stand against the Japanese 31st Division, featuring a commemorative war memorial, ancient stone monoliths, and sweeping river gorge vistas.

name: Kachai Village (Kachai Lemon GI Valley)
description: Nestled in a picturesque mountain valley in western Ukhrul district 47 km from Ukhrul town, Kachai is celebrated globally as the birthplace of the world-famous 'Kachai Lemon' (Citrus jambhiri), which holds the prestigious Geographical Indication (GI) tag for its extraordinarily high ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) content of over 51% (more than double ordinary lemons), host of the grand annual Kachai Lemon Festival every January featuring lemon exhibitions, cultural dances, and orchard tours.

name: Kachouphung Lake & Azoa Jenephiu Magi Lake
description: Situated in the remote eastern highlands of Ukhrul district approximately 7 km from Achangba along the border with Myanmar, Kachouphung Lake is a mystical high-altitude natural freshwater body covering about 9 acres, celebrated for its astonishing natural shoreline that strikingly resembles the geographical map of India, surrounded by dense pine and alder forests, aquatic lotus plants, and adjacent to the sacred Azoa Jenephiu Magi Lake renowned for breeding indigenous freshwater fish.

name: Kangkhui Lime Caves (Khangkhui Mangsor)
description: Situated in the rocky limestone hills of Kangkhui Khullen village 16 km southeast of Ukhrul town, celebrated in Indian archaeology as an invaluable Paleolithic heritage site, excavated by archaeologist O. Kumar Singh in 1969 where ancient stone tools and animal bones dating back to the Upper Paleolithic era were discovered, featuring dark, winding subterranean karst chambers, colossal calcified stalactites, stalagmites, natural limestone domes, and chambers associated with Tangkhul King Mangsor.

name: Khamasom Ancient Tangkhul Village & Orchid Slopes
description: Situated in the rugged northeastern mountain ranges of Ukhrul district near the international border with Myanmar 35 km from Ukhrul town, Khamasom is an ancient Tangkhul Naga settlement celebrated for its pristine natural mountain environment, scenic rock formations, roaring waterfall streams, blooming wild orchids, and close proximity to the high mountain ridges where wild lilies grow in untouched alpine habitats.

name: Khorung Mount (Mount Sachiri) & High Ridge Lookout
description: Soaring above the northern Chingai subdivision of Ukhrul, Khorung Mount (locally known as Mount Sachiri) is a prominent high-altitude peak that commands breathtaking 360-degree vistas stretching from the Somra tract in Myanmar to the distant Saramati range in Nagaland. The mountain is blanketed in dwarf bamboo, wild sub-alpine berries, and pine groves, providing adventurous hikers with untamed ridgeline trails.

name: Longpi Black Stone Pottery Village (Nungbi Khullen)
description: Situated 37 km north of Ukhrul town along the highway, Longpi (comprising Longpi Khullen and Longpi Kajui) is internationally celebrated by designers and anthropologists for its ancient heritage of 'Longpi Ham' (Longpi Black Stone Pottery), an extraordinary craft where master Tangkhul artisans blend pulverized black serpentine rock and weathered clay by hand into cooking pots, kettles, and teacups without using a potter's wheel, shaping them entirely with hands, moulds, and stones before open-pit bonfire firing.

name: Marangphung Saline Springs & Traditional Tangkhul Salt Well
description: Hidden in the wooded hills of northern Ukhrul, Marangphung preserves ancient natural saline water springs (Machi) that have been a cornerstone of traditional Tangkhul trade and subsistence for centuries. Indigenous villagers draw high-saline mineral brine from historic stone-lined wells and evaporate it over wood-fired hearths in earthenware vessels to produce circular salt cakes used for traditional cooking and customary gift exchanges.

name: Nillai Organic Green Tea Estate Phangrei
description: Perched on rolling mountain slopes near Phangrei 20 km north of Ukhrul town at an elevation of 1,800 meters, Nillai is a celebrated commercial agro-tourism tea estate famous for producing premium organic wild green tea and black orthodox tea, cultivated in pesticide-free mountain soil kissed by morning mist, featuring scenic hillside tea walks, artisanal tea rolling sheds, and tea-tasting sessions overlooking the Ukhrul valleys.

name: Phangrei Hill Meadows & Cold Water Fishery
description: Situated 22 km north of Ukhrul town along the road to Lunghar, Phangrei is an expansive, rolling emerald grassy plateau perched high in the clouds, celebrated in Tangkhul folklore as the romantic hill where legendary lovers Shimreishang and Maitonphi spent their youth, featuring scenic cold-water fishery ponds breeding Himalayan trout and carp, designated camping sites, and panoramic viewpoints overlooking deep pine-clad valleys.

name: Shangshak War Memorial & WWII Battlefield Ridge
description: Perched on a strategic mountain plateau in southern Ukhrul, the Shangshak War Memorial marks the hallowed ground of the fierce Battle of Shangshak (March 19-26, 1944). Here, the Indian 50th Parachute Brigade fought a heroic, desperate delaying action against the advancing Imperial Japanese 31st Division, critically buying time for the defense of Kohima and Imphal. The memorial features a commemorative stone obelisk, regiment rolls, and tranquil landscaped mountain views.

name: Shingcha Kachui (Shingcha Hill & Rhododendron Ridge)
description: Rising gracefully in southeastern Ukhrul, Shingcha Kachui is an elevated mountain ridge renowned among local trekkers for its spectacular seasonal bursts of wild crimson and pink Rhododendron arboreum blossoms during early spring. The summit offers breathtaking 360-degree panoramas of the rolling Tangkhul highlands, early morning cloud inversions, and mist-veiled mountain valleys stretching toward the international frontier.

name: Shirui Hills & Shirui Peak (Kashong Peak)
description: Rising to a majestic altitude of 2,835 meters (9,301 feet) above Shirui village 18 km east of Ukhrul town, celebrated globally as the solitary natural habitat on Earth of the rare, endangered Shirui Lily (Lilium mackliniae - the state flower of Manipur), discovered by British botanist Frank Kingdon-Ward in 1946, featuring a thrilling mountain ridge trek through cloud forests culminating in high-altitude grassy meadows that burst into pale pink, bell-shaped blooms in May-June, celebrated during the annual Shirui Lily Festival.

name: Shirui Kashong Rear Ridges & Northern Orchid Trails
description: Extending northward beyond the primary tourist trail of Shirui Kashung peak, the rear ridges of the mountain range encompass a rugged, undisturbed sub-alpine wilderness. Here, sub-tropical dwarf rhododendrons, rare endemic herbs, and wild epiphytic orchids thrive along misty granite escarpments and cloud-inversion mountain passes far removed from festival crowds.

name: Sihai Phangrei & Valley Terraces Trail
description: Extending beyond the popular Phangrei picnic plateau toward the rural villages of Sihai Khullen and Sihai Khunou, Sihai Phangrei is an enchanting mountain valley framed by rolling pine-crested ridges and cascading rice terraces. The valley is crisscrossed by unpaved walking tracks leading past crystalline mountain brooks, seasonal wildflowers, and traditional timber farm shelters offering genuine pastoral peace.

name: Sirarakhong Chilli Village (Hathei Chilli Valley)
description: Situated on scenic mountain ridges in southwestern Ukhrul district 66 km from Imphal and 30 km from Ukhrul, Sirarakhong is an enchanting Tangkhul tribal village celebrated across India for its extraordinary organic red chilli - the 'Hathei Chilli' (Sirarakhong Chilli), which received the prestigious Geographical Indication (GI) tag for its vibrant crimson color, unique aromatic pungency, and medicinal qualities that grow nowhere else with the same potency, host of the famous annual Sirarakhong Hathei Chilli Festival in August-September.

name: Talui (Tolloi) Village & Heritage Terraced Hillside
description: Sprawling across a lush mountain amphitheater in western Ukhrul, Talui (Tolloi) is one of the premier cultural and agrarian settlements of the Tangkhul community. The village is renowned for its cascading stepped rice terraces carved into green hillsides, historic Christian mission churches, cottage sericulture silk units, and progressive customary community governance.

name: Ukhrul
description: Ukhrul, the district headquarters of Ukhrul district in Manipur, is a treasure trove of natural beauty and rich cultural heritage. The village is nestled in the picturesque valley surrounded by the majestic mountains of the Indo-Burma biodiversity hotspot. With its unique blend of Tangkhul Naga traditions and breathtaking landscapes, Ukhrul offers an unforgettable experience for travelers. The town is steeped in history and culture, with many ancient monuments, festivals, and customs that showcase the resilience and hospitality of the Tangkhul people. Visitors can immerse themselves in the local way of life, explore the surrounding countryside, and take in the stunning vistas that make Ukhrul a nature lover's paradise.

name: Zingsui Terraced Village & Waterfalls Ukhrul
description: Perched on a scenic, sun-drenched mountain spur in eastern Ukhrul district 28 km from Ukhrul town, Zingsui is an idyllic Tangkhul agrarian village celebrated for its magnificent tiered mountain waterfalls tumbling through pine-forested gorges, sweeping amphitheatres of irrigated stepped terrace rice fields, and traditional wooden morungs adorned with ancestral carvings.
